├── src/anqchor/
│   ├── cli/                    # main.py (root app; match run|report|all, cis run|compare|report|all,
│   │                           # trans run|compare|report|all, run/steps/report, hidden _step),
│   │                           # options.py (shared options, flag -> config overrides), execute.py,
│   │                           # qpgen.py (build/check), prepare.py (index-pvar, pgen-list, pheno, cov)
│   ├── config/                 # model.py (pydantic models), load.py (YAML, merge, path resolution)
│   ├── engine/                 # step.py (Step, StepGraph), minimake.py (Makefile), runner.py (make), provenance.py
│   ├── qpgen/                  # locate.py, build.py, commands.py (argv builders), outputs.py (readers)
│   ├── io/                     # pheno.py, cov.py, pairs.py, genotypes.py, maps.py, tables.py
│   ├── pipelines/              # layout.py (file names), common.py, match.py, cis.py, trans.py, report.py, context.py
│   ├── steps/                  # Python step kinds: prepare.py, strategy.py, match.py, cis.py, trans.py;
│   │                           # cis_compare.py, trans_compare.py ('cis compare', 'trans compare',
│   │                           # not steps), compare.py (labels, settings copies, compare.json)
│   ├── report/                 # report step kinds (match, cis, trans, index), render.py, theme.py, templates/, static/
│   ├── stats.py                # significance predicate shared by cis and trans (p < α; BH q ≤ α)
│   └── util/                   # files.py (atomic writes, gz helpers), log.py
└── tests/
    ├── unit/                   # no qpgen needed
    ├── integration/            # test_mage.py + expected_mage.json
    └── fixtures/               # small real qpgen outputs (qpgen/), io fixtures

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
uv sync                    # Python >= 3.10, dev tools included
uv run anqchor --help

Tip

If another virtual environment is active, uv warns that VIRTUAL_ENV does not match the project environment. Run commands as env -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv run ... to use the project's .venv.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest -q                       # everything available
uv run pytest -q -m "not integration"  # unit tests only, no qpgen needed
uv run pytest -q -m integration        # the example data end to end

The integration tests run on the example data shipped in examples/mage/data/, so they need no download, only a built qpgentools (qpgen 0.2.0). They look for the binary in $ANQCHOR_QPGEN, then PATH, then extern/qpgen/bin/, and skip when none is found:

ANQCHOR_QPGEN=/opt/qpgen/bin/qpgentools uv run pytest -q -m integration

test_mage.py runs every analysis once per session, all at the same time: flag-only match run (also with --mahalanobis --lambda auto), one flag-only cis run per covariate set (nocov, basic, peer10, peer60; nocov and peer60 again with the rect engine, and peer60 on a subset of the reference), one flag-only trans run per setup (nocov, basic, peer10, peer60, peer60_rint), cis compare over the cis runs and trans compare over the trans runs. It asserts the numbers in tests/integration/expected_mage.json and the engine behaviour (re-runs, --dry-run, --only, --until, reports), including cis run → cis compare → cis report and trans run → trans compare → trans report. When qpgen or the example data change, update expected_mage.json, not the test. The example data is rebuilt from the full MAGE files with examples/mage/make_compact_data.sh.

docs.title: Lint and type checks
docs.text:
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy                  # strict on anqchor.config, anqchor.engine, anqchor.qpgen

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
uv sync --extra docs
uv run mkdocs serve
uv run mkdocs build --strict

The configuration reference is written from config/model.py, the CLI reference from --help, and the output reference from fresh runs on the example data (pipelines/layout.py and the step modules); update them together with the code. The reports are being redesigned, so the pages carry no report screenshots for now.

docs.title: Foundation contracts
docs.text:
These rules keep the pieces independent; reviews check them.

  1. qpgen does the numerics. No statistical re-implementation of what qpgen computes; Python does orchestration, normalisation, summaries and reports.
  2. qpgen flags appear only in qpgen/commands.py; qpgen output layouts only in qpgen/outputs.py.
  3. File names come only from pipelines/layout.py.
  4. A step reads only its declared inputs and params and writes every declared output atomically. Every parameter that changes a result is in params (so it is in the signature and re-runs the step).
  5. Reports are rendered from summaries (TSV/JSON with schema_version), never from raw qpgen output.
  6. Config is the single source of truth. Flags build a config; the resolved config is written to the run directory. Unknown keys are errors.
  7. anqchor always hands qpgen regenie-layout matrices and a 4-column pgen list with absolute prefixes.
  8. The generated Makefile stays GNU make 3.81 compatible (no grouped targets, .SHELLFLAGS or $(file …)).

docs.title: Adding a step or a pipeline
docs.text:
• A step: add its file names to Layout, implement the kind with @register (module listed in anqchor.steps.STEP_MODULES), emit the Step from the pipeline's build(), add unit tests. See Python API.
  • A pipeline: add pipelines/<name>.py with build(ctx) -> list[Step] and REPORT_STEP, add it to PIPELINES, add a config model under PipelinesConfig, run, report and all commands in cli/main.py, a report kind and the index tile, and integration expectations.
  • A config key: add it to the pydantic model with a docstring, pass it through the step params, document it in docs/user-guide/configuration.md, add a unit test.
  • A qpgen flag: add it to the builder in qpgen/commands.py and its test.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
• CHANGELOG.md updated; version in pyproject.toml (__version__ is read from the installed metadata).
  • Full test suite green with the pinned extern/qpgen commit; expected_mage.json current.
  • mkdocs build --strict clean.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: anqchor is a Python package (Python ≥ 3.10) plus the qpgen C++ toolkit, which is vendored as a git submodule (extern/qpgen, branch dev) and built from the checkout. anqchor is not on PyPI yet; install it from a clone.

docs.title: 1. Clone with submodules
docs.text:
git clone --recursive https://github.com/statgen/anqchor.git
cd anqchor
# already cloned without --recursive?
git submodule update --init --recursive

The second command also fetches qpgen's own submodules (htslib, qgenlib, Eigen).

docs.title: 2. Install the Python package
docs.text:
uv (recommended)pip 
uv sync                 # creates .venv with anqchor and the dev tools
uv run anqchor --version

Run every command as uv run anqchor ..., or activate .venv.

python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .
anqchor --version

Runtime dependencies: typer, pydantic (v2), pyyaml, pandas, numpy, scipy, plotly, jinja2. anqchor also needs GNU make (3.81 or later; the macOS default works) on PATH, or in $ANQCHOR_MAKE.

docs.title: 3. Build qpgen
docs.text:
anqchor qpgen build -j 8

This runs qpgen's documented three-stage build inside extern/qpgen: htslib (autoreconf -i, ./configure, make), qgenlib (cmake, make), then qpgen itself (cmake, make). Stages whose artefacts already exist are skipped; --force rebuilds htslib and qgenlib too. The output is extern/qpgen/bin/qpgentools, and the full log is extern/qpgen/anqchor-build.log.

Build requirements: a C++14 compiler with OpenMP, cmake, make, autoreconf, and the compression libraries htslib uses (zlib, bzip2, lzma; optionally libdeflate, libcurl, libcrypto). LAPACK/BLAS are optional.

macOS

Apple Clang has no OpenMP. Install it and Homebrew LLVM before building:

brew install libomp llvm cmake autoconf automake

qpgen's CMake configuration selects Homebrew LLVM automatically. anqchor qpgen build warns before building when libomp or a Homebrew LLVM is missing. Extra CMake settings can be passed with --cmake-arg (repeatable), for example --cmake-arg=-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang++.

Using a qpgen binary built elsewhere

You do not have to build from the submodule. anqchor looks for qpgentools in this order:

  1. --qpgen PATH (root option) or qpgen.binary in the config;
  2. the ANQCHOR_QPGEN environment variable;
  3. qpgentools on PATH;
  4. extern/qpgen/bin/qpgentools of the source checkout.

An explicit path or ANQCHOR_QPGEN that does not name an executable is an error (exit code 4); anqchor does not silently fall back to another binary.

docs.title: 4. Check the installation
docs.text:
anqchor qpgen check

binary:   /path/to/anqchor/extern/qpgen/bin/qpgentools  (found via submodule)
sha256:   <sha256 of your build>
commit:   5b811e250591931cd80f9a7dfae80d47eb8381e2
status:   ok (pair-prs, match-prs-pheno, pair-assoc, rect-assoc available)

The command checks that the four subcommands anqchor uses exist. It prints the binary's sha256 and the git commit of the checkout the binary sits in. The same information is recorded in every run's run.json.

Then check the qpgen version:

extern/qpgen/bin/qpgentools --version
# qpgentools 0.2.0 (git 5b811e2)

anqchor needs qpgen 0.2.0 or later

qpgen 0.2.0 fixed several problems in the association and matching tools that change anqchor's numbers. The most important: pair-assoc now adjusts the genotypes for the covariates as well as the phenotypes, all association tools use df = N - 2 - k with k covariates, and non-numeric covariate values such as XX/XY are an error (unless the covariate is named with --cat-cov-names) instead of being read as 0. Older builds give different, and with many covariates optimistic, results. anqchor also passes --cat-cov-names for categorical covariates such as sex, which needs qpgen commit 5b811e2 or later (the pinned submodule); an older 0.2.0 build does not accept that option, and anqchor qpgen check reports it as missing options. anqchor qpgen check does not read the version, so run qpgentools --version yourself. Builds before 0.2.0 have no --version option at all. Details: qpgen integration.

docs.title: 5. Run the example
docs.text: The repository ships a small example dataset in examples/mage/data/. The quickstart runs the quickest analysis on it in about 10 seconds; if that works, the installation is complete.

docs.title: Other tools
docs.text:
• bgzip and tabix (htslib) are needed by anqchor prepare index-pvar to create indexed pvar files, and make the reference presence check faster (without tabix anqchor reads the whole pvar instead). anqchor looks for them in $ANQCHOR_BGZIP / $ANQCHOR_TABIX, then on PATH, then in the htslib built inside extern/qpgen/submodules/htslib.
  • zstd on PATH is needed only to index a .pvar.zst.

docs.title: Building this documentation
docs.text:
uv sync --extra docs
uv run mkdocs serve          # http://127.0.0.1:8000
uv run mkdocs build --strict # static site in site/

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This page takes you from a fresh installation to a first result in a few minutes. It runs the quickest analysis, sample identity matching, on the example data that ships with the repository. Every command is run from the repository root, and every number below comes from an actual run with qpgen 0.2.0.

docs.title: 1. Check the installation
docs.text:
anqchor --version            # anqchor 0.1.0.dev0
anqchor qpgen check          # status: ok (pair-prs, match-prs-pheno, pair-assoc, rect-assoc available)
extern/qpgen/bin/qpgentools --version   # qpgentools 0.2.0 (git 5b811e2)

If anqchor is not found, prefix the commands with uv run or activate .venv. If qpgen check fails, see Installation.

docs.title: 2. The question
docs.text:
Every omics sample in an xQTL study carries a label that says which genotyped individual it came from. Sample swaps, mislabelled tubes and contaminated libraries break that link, and a broken link weakens every association you test later.

Identity matching checks each link with the genetics itself. Known cis-eQTL effects, applied to an individual's genotypes, predict that individual's expression of each gene. Across hundreds of genes the predicted profile of a person matches their own measured profile far better than anyone else's. anqchor compares every expression sample against every genotyped individual and reports whether the labelled individual is the best match.

flowchart TB
  K[("367 known<br/>cis-eQTLs")] --> P["Predicted expression<br/>per individual"]
  G["Genotypes<br/>729 individuals"] --> P
  P --> M["Compare with<br/>measured expression"]
  E["Expression<br/>729 samples x 367 genes"] --> M
  M --> V["Per-sample verdict"]

docs.title: 3. The inputs
docs.text:
The example data in examples/mage/data/ (32 MB) comes from the MAGE RNA-seq study of 1000 Genomes lymphoblastoid cell lines, restricted to chromosomes 21 and 22. The example data page describes how it was built. Identity matching uses four files.

Genotypes: a qpgen pgen list naming one PLINK2 file set per chromosome. Each set has a .pgen, a .psam and an indexed pvar (.pvar.idx.gz + .tbi). Together: 729 individuals × 256,645 variants with minor allele frequency ≥ 5%.

$ cat examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv
21  1   1000000000  mage_chr21
22  1   1000000000  mage_chr22
$ head -3 examples/mage/data/geno/mage_chr21.psam
#IID
HG00096
HG00100

The columns of the pgen list are CHROM BEG END PREFIX. A relative prefix is found next to the list file.

Expression: one row per sample, one column per gene (the regenie layout). 729 samples × 367 genes.

$ gzip -dc examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz | head -3 | cut -f1-4
FID IID ENSG00000275993.3:SIK1B ENSG00000278931.1:bP-2189O9.2
HG00096 HG00096 -0.238523   0.224454
HG00100 HG00100 -0.217436   -0.309645

Covariates: the same layout. Sex (XX/XY, a categorical covariate that qpgen encodes itself; anqchor passes --cat-cov-names sex), 5 genotype principal components and 60 PEER factors: 66 covariates. Identity matching removes their effect from the expression before comparing.

$ gzip -dc examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz | head -3 | cut -f1-8
FID IID sex PC1 PC2 PC3 PC4 PC5
HG00096 HG00096 XY  -0.0216243  0.0487524   0.00362148  0.0446186   0.00187148
HG00100 HG00100 XX  -0.0215191  0.0503942   0.00281614  0.040869    0.000118772

Known xQTLs (the reference): one row per gene–variant pair. 367 cis-eQTLs from GTEx (EBV-transformed lymphocytes, the same cell type as MAGE, in donors who are not MAGE individuals), one per gene: the gene's strongest (sentinel) variant. variant is CHROM:POS:REF:ALT and beta is the effect of the ALT allele.

$ gzip -dc examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz | head -3
trait   variant beta    se  pval
ENSG00000275993.3:SIK1B 21:6122794:C:T  -0.448959   0.0888711   8.054e-07
ENSG00000278931.1:bP-2189O9.2   21:9370164:G:A  0.484109    0.10423 5.31901e-06

Here the expression sample IDs equal the genotype IDs, so no sample map is needed. With your own data, --sample-map gives a geno_id pheno_id table (see Inputs).

docs.title: 4. Run the analysis
docs.text:
anqchor match run \
  --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --cov examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --out results/match

[anqchor] running prepare.genotypes
[anqchor] running prepare.reference.reference
[anqchor] running prepare.dataset.dataset
[anqchor] running prepare.mapping.dataset.reference
[anqchor] running prs.reference
[anqchor] running match.dataset.qpgen
[anqchor] running match.dataset.summarize
ran: prepare.genotypes, prepare.reference.reference, prepare.dataset.dataset, prepare.mapping.dataset.reference, prs.reference, match.dataset.qpgen, match.dataset.summarize

This takes about 7 seconds on a laptop. anqchor checks the inputs, computes a polygenic score for every individual and gene (qpgentools pair-prs), scores every sample against every individual (qpgentools match-prs-pheno) and writes summary tables. Without a configuration file the dataset is called dataset and the reference reference; these names appear in step and directory names.

match run writes no HTML. Render the report from the tables, which takes about a second and runs no analysis:

anqchor match report --out results/match
# match report: results/match/report/match.html

anqchor match all with the same flags does both in one command. Run the same match run command again and nothing is recomputed (ran: nothing (all steps up to date)).

docs.title: 5. The outputs
docs.text:
results/match/
├── anqchor.resolved.yaml     every setting of this run (re-run it with --config)
├── run.json                  provenance: anqchor version, qpgen binary and commit, commands, timings
├── match/dataset/
│   ├── summary.json          verdict and counts
│   ├── samples.tsv           one row per expression sample
│   ├── swaps.tsv             samples that match another individual
│   ├── candidates.tsv        unlabelled samples with a clear match (rescue candidates)
│   ├── related.tsv           samples with several close matches (possible relatives)
│   └── weights.tsv           how much each gene contributes
├── report/match.html         the interactive report (after 'match report')
├── prepare/  prs/            prepared inputs and polygenic scores
└── logs/  steps/  Makefile   step logs and bookkeeping

Every file and column is described in Output files.

docs.title: 6. Interpret the result
docs.text:
The verdict in summary.json (the report shows the same counts as tiles):

727 of 729 mapped samples confirmed (14 only leniently); 2 unclear
Status Group In the report Samples Meaning SELF_BEST PASS Strict match 713 the labelled individual is the best match SELF_LENIENT WARN Lenient match 14 the labelled individual is not the best match, but its Z-score is above 1.96 UNCLEAR WARN Own ID too weak 2 the labelled individual is not the best match and scores at most 1.96, and no other individual is clearly better

The two unclear samples, from samples.tsv:

pheno_id z_self rank_self best_id z_best z_gap NA11919 0.41 253 HG00237 3.60 0.32 NA12717 1.94 13 NA19404 2.71 0.03

The expression labelled NA11919 does not match its own genotypes: rank 253 of 729, at the level of an unrelated individual, while correctly labelled samples typically reach Z ≈ 5.5. Its best candidate, HG00237, is only 0.32 ahead of the next, which is not a clear match (the default asks for a lead of 2), so anqchor names no new ID. The label is probably wrong, but the true source is unknown: someone not genotyped here, a mixture or a poor library. For NA12717 every candidate, its own included, is at background level: weak signal rather than evidence of a wrong label.

In a real study you would now look at the lab records for NA11919, and leave it out of the xQTL analysis until it is resolved.

related.tsv lists 8 samples that have a second individual close behind the best match: usually relatives. They are informational, not errors, and the report does not show them.

docs.title: 7. What to try next
docs.text:
• Change the thresholds: --z-threshold 2.5 (lenient match) or --z-diff 3 (clear new best), then match run again. Only the matching steps re-run.
  • Score correlated genes jointly with --mahalanobis (slower, matches better here: Independent vs Mahalanobis scoring).
  • Walk through the full identity use case: Sample identity.
  • Compare covariate choices by how many known cis-eQTLs replicate: Comparing cis runs.
  • Evaluate a trans setup (replicated pairs, hotspots, inflation): trans evaluation.
  • Use your own data: Inputs, Running.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Message Cause and fix error: give --config FILE, or the input flags (see --help) No input flags were given. Add --geno-list (or --pfile), --pheno and --pairs. Invalid value for '--pheno': File '...' does not exist. A path is wrong. Paths given as flags are relative to the current directory: run from the repository root. qpgentools not found (tried: ...) (exit code 4) qpgen is not built or not found. Run anqchor qpgen build, or pass --qpgen PATH. error: another anqchor command is running in ... (exit code 2) Two commands wrote to the same --out directory at once. Wait, or use another --out. error: run failed in step <name>; log: ... (exit code 3) A step failed. The last log lines are printed above the error; the full log is in logs/<name>.log. ... is not an anqchor run directory (no anqchor.resolved.yaml) match report --out names a directory that match run has not written.

docs.title: cis: power by replication of known pairs
docs.text:
Question: how many known cis-xQTLs does an analysis setup recover in my data, and which of several setups recovers the most?

A setup is one set of inputs: genotypes, phenotypes (and their normalization), covariates, the phenotype transform (as given, or RINT with --rint) and the reference of known pairs. Each reference pair (trait, variant) is re-tested in the study data. The number of pairs that replicate, at several strengths, is a cheap and direct measure of cis-mapping power. You evaluate each setup in its own run and then compare the runs, before any genome-wide scan.

For a worked example on the MAGE data, see cis evaluation: comparing analysis setups.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  A["cis run<br/>setup A"] --> C["cis compare"]
  B["cis run<br/>setup B"] --> C
  D["cis run<br/>setup C"] --> C
  C --> T["comparison tables"]
  C --> H["report/cis.html"]
Command What it does HTML anqchor cis run tests the reference pairs for one setup and writes the summary tables of that run no anqchor cis compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR compares any finished runs, writes comparison tables yes (--no-report to skip) anqchor cis report --out DIR re-renders report/cis.html of a comparison or of a single run from its tables (about 1 s, never runs qpgen) yes anqchor cis all cis run and then cis report on the same run directory yes

Runs are independent: start them in parallel, each into its own --out directory. Runs may differ in any input, not only in covariates. A run tests one phenotype transform: the phenotypes as given (default), or with --rint a rank-based inverse normal transform after covariate adjustment. To see what RINT changes, make a second run with --rint and compare the two; phenotypes that are already inverse-normal transformed need no RINT run.

A run is described by flags (a configuration file is optional):

anqchor cis run \
    --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
    --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --cov examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 \
    --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
    --out results/cis/peer10
Flag Meaning --geno-list or --pfile genotypes: a qpgen pgen list, or one PLINK2 prefix with .pgen/.psam/.pvar.idx.gz --pheno, --pheno-format phenotype matrix (default format regenie) --cov, --cov-format covariate matrix. Omit --cov to run without covariates --cat-cov-names categorical covariates coded as numbers (e.g. a batch number); non-numeric columns such as sex are categorical automatically --cov-include use only these covariates of --cov: comma-separated names; ranges such as PEER1-10 expand to PEER1 … PEER10. Default: every covariate in --cov --pairs reference pairs: trait variant beta se [pval] --trait-annot trait loci (BED-like). Needed only to split the rect engine's controls by chromosome --trait-id-rule how reference trait IDs map onto phenotype columns (default as_is) --rint apply a rank-based inverse normal transform (RINT) to the phenotypes after covariate adjustment. Default: the phenotypes as given --assoc-engine pair (default, pair-assoc) or rect (rect-assoc)

The same run can be written as a configuration file, for example examples/mage/cis.yaml (the all-covariate run): anqchor cis run --config examples/mage/cis.yaml --out results/cis_config. See Configuration for every key.

docs.title: Steps of a run
docs.text:
With flags only, the dataset is called dataset, the reference reference and the run's single strategy default (set --dataset-name / --reference-name to change the first two). Step names below use <ds>, <ref> and <s> for them.

Step Kind What it does prepare.genotypes Python genotype samples, normalized pgen list prepare.reference.<ref> Python reads the reference pairs, checks which variants are in the genotypes prepare.dataset.<ds> Python normalizes phenotypes and covariates (categorical covariates such as sex keep their text levels XX/XY; qpgen encodes them) prepare.mapping.<ds>.<ref> Python maps reference traits onto phenotype columns cis.<ds>.<s>.inputs Python the run's covariate file (all of --cov, the --cov-include subset, or none) and strategy.json cis.<ds>.<s>.assoc (pair engine) qpgen one pair-assoc run over the mapped pairs (--skip-rint unless --rint) cis.<ds>.<s>.rect.<t> (rect engine) qpgen one rect-assoc run over the reference's present variants × mapped traits; <t> is raw, or rint with --rint cis.<ds>.summarize Python replication levels, per-trait table, power curve, summary report.cis Python report/cis.html; only with cis all or cis report

The qpgen command of the all-covariate MAGE run (from the run's Makefile; paths are relative to the run directory):

qpgentools pair-assoc --pgen-list prepare/genotypes/pgen_list.tsv \
    --pheno prepare/datasets/dataset/pheno.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --pairs prepare/datasets/dataset/ref.reference/pairs.tsv.gz \
    --out cis/dataset/strategies/default/pair_assoc.tsv.gz \
    --cov cis/dataset/strategies/default/cov.regenie.tsv.gz --cat-cov-names sex --skip-rint

With --rint the command has no --skip-rint, and the summary reads qpgen's *_RINT columns. With --assoc-engine rect and --rint:

qpgentools rect-assoc --pgen-list prepare/genotypes/pgen_list.tsv \
    --pheno prepare/datasets/dataset/pheno.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --var-list prepare/datasets/dataset/ref.reference/variants.txt \
    --out cis/dataset/strategies/default/rect_assoc.rint.tsv.gz \
    --cov cis/dataset/strategies/default/cov.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --pheno-list prepare/datasets/dataset/ref.reference/traits.txt --cat-cov-names sex --rint-after-adj

Without covariates --cov is left out. --cat-cov-names lists the categorical covariates among the run's covariates: non-numeric columns such as sex plus any named with --cat-cov-names (for categories coded as numbers, e.g. a batch number). qpgen encodes each as L − 1 indicator columns. --cov-include sex,PC1-5 passes --cat-cov-names sex; --cov-include PC1-5,PEER1-10 passes none. anqchor needs qpgen 0.2.0 or later (qpgen integration).

docs.title: Model and transform
docs.text:
• Phenotypes as given (default): the phenotype and the genotype are both residualized on the covariates (with an intercept; Frisch-Waugh-Lovell), then regressed on each other. beta is the partial effect of the genotype, as in y ~ 1 + covariates + genotype.
  • --rint: the covariate-adjusted phenotype is rank-based inverse-normal transformed (Blom offsets, average ranks for ties) and tested the same way. pair-assoc's *_RINT columns correspond to rect-assoc --rint-after-adj. RINT rescales the phenotype, so its effect sizes are not on the reference's scale; compare z-scores or −log10 p instead.
  • Degrees of freedom: df = N − 2 − k, where N is the number of samples and k the rank of the covariate matrix; N − 2 without covariates.

docs.title: Engines
docs.text:
pair (default) tests exactly the reference pairs. rect tests the whole rectangle of reference variants × reference traits (346 × 367 = 126,982 cells on MAGE) and keeps the non-reference cells as local controls: their λ_GC and p < 1e-5 counts appear in strategies.tsv (*_control* columns), overall and for cross-chromosome cells (these need --trait-annot). Same-chromosome control cells are in LD with neighbouring eQTLs, so they are not a null; the cross-chromosome cells are much closer to one.

On MAGE both engines give identical replication counts at every level for the example runs (with and without --rint), and identical per-pair statistics.

docs.title: Replication levels
docs.text:
Each tested pair gets one 0/1 flag per level. Every level requires sign concordance (sign(beta_ref) == sign(beta)); alleles agree by construction because the reference variant ID (CHROM:POS:REF:ALT) is the tested variant and beta is the effect of ALT.

Level Default rule Cut-off on MAGE (367 pairs) sign sign concordance only none nominal sign and p < 0.05 −log10 p > 1.30 fdr sign and Benjamini-Hochberg q ≤ 0.05 over the run's tested pairs data-dependent bonferroni sign and p < 0.05 / n_tested 0.05/367 → −log10 p > 3.87 strict sign and p < 1e-5 −log10 p > 5

The levels are configurable in a configuration file (pipelines.cis.levels; null switches one off).

Level order. Levels are ranked by their actual −log10 p cut-off, not by name: with 367 pairs Bonferroni (p < 1.36e-4) is weaker than strict, but with tens of thousands of pairs it is stronger. summary.json level_order records the order used.

Status. Every mapped pair has a status: tested, variant_absent (variant not in the genotypes) or not_tested (present but no qpgen result or no finite statistic, for example a variant with no variation among the phenotyped samples). The summary step fails when more than max_unresolved_fraction (20%) of the mapped pairs are unresolved, because the result would then say more about variant matching than about power. The error names absent examples; a different genome build, chr21 vs 21, swapped REF/ALT or a different indel representation are the usual causes.

Recommendation (comparison). The run with the most pairs at the strongest level (by default strict), ties broken by the next weaker levels, then by order. summary.json and the report state the reason in words.

z-scores and effective sample size. Every tested pair has a signed z = beta / se and the reference's z_ref = beta_ref / se_ref; both refer to the same allele. For a pair, E[z²] ≈ 1 + N·β²·Var(g)/σ²ₑ (the noncentrality), with σ²ₑ the residual variance, so on the same pairs (mean z² − 1) is proportional to the effective sample size: removing residual variance with covariates shrinks se and raises z² as more samples would. (The normal quantile of the p-value would understate strong pairs, whose p-values come from a t distribution.) rel_neff in strategies.tsv is (mean z² − 1) / (baseline mean z² − 1) over the pairs tested in every run, the baseline being the first run. It is a ratio of means, so pairs count in proportion to their z²: the strongest pairs dominate (in the MAGE example the top 10 of 367 pairs carry about a third of Σz², and the median per-pair ratio is larger than rel_neff for the stronger runs). The reference pairs are selected known signals, not a random set of variants, so it is a relative diagnostic, not a sample size. cis compare re-derives z from each run's beta and se, so every compared run uses the same definition.

π1 is Storey's 1 − π0 with a single λ = 0.5: approximate, only indicative for a few hundred pairs.

docs.title: Outputs of a run
docs.text:
results/cis/peer10/
├── cis/dataset/
│   ├── strategies.tsv          one row: counts per level, rint, mean z², ...
│   ├── pairs.long.tsv.gz       one row per reference pair (beta, z, −log10 p, reference values)
│   ├── traits.tsv              one row per trait
│   ├── power_curve.tsv         replicated count vs −log10 p threshold
│   ├── summary.json            everything above, levels, recommendation, warnings
│   └── strategies/default/     cov.regenie.tsv.gz, strategy.json, pair_assoc.tsv.gz
├── prepare/                    normalized inputs
├── logs/<step>.log             output of each step
├── steps/                      step stamps and run times (<step>.seconds)
├── anqchor.resolved.yaml       the complete settings of the run, flags included
└── run.json                    provenance: anqchor version, qpgen binary and commit, commands, host

A run writes no HTML; anqchor cis report --out results/cis/peer10 renders report/cis.html for it. Rows are labelled (run column) with the run directory name, here peer10. Column definitions: Output files. pval_ref is the reference's pval column (NA when the file has none; another column name needs columns: {pval: NAME} in a configuration file).

Reproducing a run. anqchor.resolved.yaml holds every setting, including the flags:

anqchor cis run --config results/cis/peer10/anqchor.resolved.yaml --out results/cis/peer10_again

gives identical tables (labelled peer10_again).

docs.title: Outputs of a comparison
docs.text:
anqchor cis compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR [--label L ...] [--no-report] reads finished runs (it never runs qpgen; about 1 s). Each run gets a label: the run directory name, or the --label values in order (one per run). The comparison directory holds:

File Content runs.tsv one row per run: label, run directory, genotypes and sample count, phenotypes and sample counts, covariate file, cov_include (all when every covariate was used), n_cov, covariate columns, rint, reference, engine, mapped pairs strategies.tsv one row per run (run = label = the run label): the run's own counts (n_tested, n_rep_<level>, frac_rep_<level>, median_log10p, mean_z2, beta_corr, pi1, ...), plus n_common_tested, n_rep_<level>_common, mean_z2_common and rel_neff (effective sample size relative to the first run) pairs.long.tsv.gz the runs' long tables stacked (run = label), with levels re-derived using the first run's level settings traits.tsv one row per trait, best_log10p:/level:/delta_log10p:<run> (delta against the first run), best_run power_curve.tsv per run: replicated pairs at −log10 p thresholds 0, 0.5, 1, … summary.json as for a run, plus runs, comparability (same_reference, a hash of each run's reference, rint per run) and recommended compare.json manifest of the comparison (runs, labels, command); cis report uses it to recognise a comparison directory settings/<label>.anqchor.yaml the exact settings of each compared run (a copy of its anqchor.resolved.yaml) report/cis.html the report (unless --no-report)

Common pairs. Runs can test different pairs (a different reference, or a genotype set missing some variants). n_common_tested is the number of pairs (matched by reference trait and variant) tested in every compared run, and n_rep_<level>_common counts replication over those pairs only, with FDR and Bonferroni recomputed on them. When the runs tested the same pairs, the _common columns equal the plain ones. Runs may differ in the phenotype transform: each run's rows carry its own statistics, and runs.tsv records rint. anqchor warns when the runs used different reference files or tested different pairs; then compare the _common columns. The recommendation and the report's charts use each run's own counts.

docs.title: Reading the report
docs.text:
The same page shows one run or a comparison (title Comparing N runs); the first run of a comparison is the baseline. From top to bottom:

  1. Replicated pairs by p-value threshold: the power curve. Pairs replicated (same sign, p < 10^−t, as the levels) against t on a log(1 + t) axis labelled in −log10 p, one line per run; dotted lines at the nominal and strict cut-offs and at the number of tested pairs. Count or percentage.
  2. Signal strength: for a comparison first the effective sample size relative to the baseline (rel_neff, a dot per run on a log axis around ×1, with a 95% paired bootstrap interval), then |z| or −log10 p per run as boxes (middle half, 5th–95th percentile, median) with the reference study as a hollow box, all over the pairs tested in every run.
  3. Significant hits: per run (rows), the pairs of the same sign, at the nominal and at the strict cut-off, with percentages and bars. FDR and Bonferroni counts are in the run details.
  4. Agreement with the reference: for one run at a time, effect size, z and −log10 p against the reference (each axis on its own scale; a dashed least-squares line through 0 with its slope for effect size and z), and (comparison) z against the baseline run with the line y = x. Open diamonds mark pairs with the opposite sign to the reference (against the baseline: pairs where the two runs disagree in sign).
  5. All pairs: −log10 p in the reference and in each run, with the number of runs of opposite sign; a run's value is red with a minus sign where its effect has the opposite sign (100 rows a page, sortable, searchable, header and pair column pinned).
  6. Run details (collapsed): covariates, RINT, samples, FDR and Bonferroni counts and saved settings per run; the FDR and Bonferroni rules; local controls (rect engine); untested pairs; a link to strategies.tsv with every per-run number.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
• Compare the strict and bonferroni counts. sign and nominal saturate when the reference eQTLs are strong, so they show that the data are sound but cannot rank setups.
  • A difference of a few pairs out of hundreds is within noise; prefer the simpler setup unless the power curves separate over a wide range of thresholds.
  • More replications is not always better: a setup that ignores population structure inflates every statistic and also "replicates" more. Check calibration with the rect engine's cross-chromosome controls.
  • RINT matters little for expression that is already normalized and more for skewed phenotypes (proteins, metabolites). Test it as a separate --rint run.
  • A low beta_corr or many sign-discordant pairs with an otherwise good setup point to a trait-mapping problem or a reference from a different tissue or population.
  • If the reference was discovered in the same samples with the same covariates, the setup that reproduces the discovery model is favoured by construction. Use an independent reference (for example GTEx for the same tissue, as in the MAGE example) for real decisions.

docs.title: Several strategies in one configuration file
docs.text: A configuration file may still list several entries under pipelines.cis.strategies; they are then evaluated in one run directory, and cis compare labels them <label>:<strategy>. Separate runs are simpler and can differ in any input, so this page and the example use one setup per run.

docs.title: match: sample identity
docs.text:
Question: does each omics sample come from the genotyped individual it is labelled with?

This page is the reference for the identity check: commands, steps, the qpgen calls, the status rules and every output file. For a guided walk-through on the example data, see the identity matching use case.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Known xQTL effects applied to the genotypes give every genotyped individual a predicted value (a polygenic score, PRS) for each reference trait. qpgen's match-prs-pheno correlates each omics sample's measured traits with every individual's PRS profile. It weights each trait by how well its PRS predicts it, turns the correlations into Z-scores across all genotyped individuals, and checks whether the labelled genotype is the best match.

flowchart TB
  R[("Reference pairs<br/>trait variant beta se")] --> P
  G["Genotypes"] --> P["pair-prs:<br/>PRS per individual and trait"]
  P --> M["match-prs-pheno:<br/>Z of every individual<br/>for every omics sample"]
  O["Omics matrix<br/>(+ covariates)"] --> M
  M --> S["summarize:<br/>calls, swaps, relatives"]
  S --> H["match report:<br/>report/match.html"]

Genotyped individuals without omics data are scored too. They make it possible to name the true source of a mislabelled sample and to rescue omics samples that have no genotype label.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command What it does anqchor match run prepares the inputs, computes the PRS, runs the matching and writes the summary tables. It writes no HTML. anqchor match report --out RUN_DIR renders report/match.html from the summary tables of a finished run, in about a second. It never runs qpgen. anqchor match all match run followed by match report.

Inputs are given as flags; a configuration file (--config) is optional:

anqchor match run \
  --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno     examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --cov       examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs     examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --out results/match
anqchor match report --out results/match
Flag Meaning Default --geno-list / --pfile genotypes: a qpgen pgen list, or one PLINK2 prefix with .pgen, .psam, .pvar.idx.gz required --pheno, --pheno-format omics matrix and its layout required, regenie --cov, --cov-format covariates regressed out of the omics data before matching none, regenie --cat-cov-names categorical covariates coded as numbers (e.g. a batch number); non-numeric columns such as sex are categorical automatically none --pairs reference pairs (trait variant beta se [pval]) required --sample-map geno_id pheno_id table when omics IDs differ from genotype IDs identical IDs --trait-id-rule how omics trait IDs relate to reference trait IDs as_is --use-cov / --no-use-cov adjust for --cov before matching on --rint / --no-rint rank-based inverse normal transform after the adjustment on --mahalanobis / --independent whiten correlated traits, or score them as independent independent --lambda with --mahalanobis: auto or a value in [0, 1] auto --z-threshold Z above which a non-best own genotype is a lenient match 1.96 --z-diff Z gap that makes a leading genotype a clear match 2.0 --prs-samples file of genotype IDs to use as candidates all genotyped individuals --dataset-name, --reference-name names used in output paths with flag-only inputs dataset, reference --threads threads for match-prs-pheno (changing it re-runs nothing) 1

The configuration keys of the same settings are under pipelines.match and datasets.<name> (Configuration). examples/mage/match.yaml is a complete example. Every run directory also holds anqchor.resolved.yaml, the full settings of the run including those given as flags, so

anqchor match run --config results/match/anqchor.resolved.yaml --out results/match_again

repeats a run exactly. run.json records the command line, the qpgen binary and the time of each step.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
<ref> and <ds> are the reference and dataset names (reference and dataset with flag-only inputs).

Step Kind What it does Run by prepare.genotypes Python checks the genotype files; writes an absolute pgen list and the sample list run, all prepare.reference.<ref> Python normalises the reference pairs; checks which variants exist in the genotypes run, all prepare.dataset.<ds> Python converts the omics matrix and covariates to regenie layout (categorical covariates such as sex keep their text levels); reads the sample map run, all prepare.mapping.<ds>.<ref> Python maps reference traits onto omics traits run, all prs.<ref> qpgen pair-prs over all genotyped individuals (or --prs-samples) run, all match.<ds>.qpgen Python + qpgen restricts the trait and sample maps to what the PRS and the omics matrix contain, decides λ, runs match-prs-pheno run, all match.<ds>.summarize Python per-sample calls, swaps, rescue candidates, relatives, weights, summary.json run, all report.match Python report/match.html report, all

Re-running with the same settings runs nothing. Changing only --z-threshold, --z-diff, --rint, --use-cov, --mahalanobis or --lambda re-runs match.<ds>.qpgen and match.<ds>.summarize; the prepared inputs and the PRS are reused. After such a re-run, run anqchor match report again: an existing report/match.html is not updated by match run, which then prints match report: ... is older than the results; update it with 'anqchor match report --out DIR'.

docs.title: The qpgen calls
docs.text:
From the example run above (paths relative to the run directory):

qpgentools pair-prs --pgen-list prepare/genotypes/pgen_list.tsv \
    --pairs prepare/references/reference/pairs.tsv.gz --out prs/reference/prs
qpgentools match-prs-pheno --prs prs/reference/prs.prs.tsv.gz \
    --pheno prepare/datasets/dataset/pheno.regenie.tsv.gz --out match/dataset/qpgen \
    --cov prepare/datasets/dataset/cov.regenie.tsv.gz --cat-cov-names sex \
    --rint --z-threshold 1.96 --z-diff 2 --threads 1

--cat-cov-names lists the categorical covariates of the file: the non-numeric ones (here sex, XX/XY) plus any named with anqchor's --cat-cov-names (config datasets.<ds>.cov_categorical), for example a batch number. qpgen encodes each as L − 1 indicator columns (covariates). Without --cov (or with --no-use-cov) both flags are left out.

Flags added when needed: --sample on pair-prs with --prs-samples; --sample-tsv with a sample map; --trait-tsv when reference and omics trait IDs differ; --mahalanobis with --auto-lambda or --lambda X; --min-weight; --missing-str. The --out prefix is a temporary directory inside match/dataset/ (shown as match/dataset/qpgen above). The exact command of a run is in match/<ds>/qpgen.params.json (argv) and at the top of logs/match.<ds>.qpgen.log.

docs.title: Scoring: independence (default) or Mahalanobis
docs.text:
By default traits are scored as independent, the fast path. With --mahalanobis (mahalanobis: true) qpgen whitens correlated traits:

  • --lambda auto (the default) uses qpgen's --auto-lambda when at least min_self_for_auto (100) samples are mapped. With fewer, anqchor uses --lambda 0.5 and says so in the log, summary.json warnings and the report.
  • a number in [0, 1] is passed as --lambda. λ = 1 is equivalent to independence.

--lambda without --mahalanobis is accepted and has no effect. On the example data, auto-λ tunes to 0.58 and confirms 11 more samples strictly than independence scoring (details).

docs.title: Status rules
docs.text:
anqchor ports qpgen's MatchStatus rules line by line, and the report ports them to JavaScript; shared test vectors pin both. With Z(1) ≥ … ≥ Z(5) the top five Z-scores, t = z_threshold and d = z_diff, checked in order:

  1. NO_OBS_TRAITS: no observed trait with non-zero weight.
  2. SELF_BEST: mapped, and the labelled genotype ranks first.
  3. SINGLE_NEW_BEST: Z(1) > Z(2) + d.
  4. MULTI_NEW_BEST: Z(k) > Z(k+1) + d for some k in 2..4.
  5. SELF_LENIENT: mapped and Z.self > t.
  6. UNCLEAR when mapped, NO_SELF otherwise.

Both comparisons are strict: a gap of exactly z_diff is not clear.

Group Statuses Meaning PASS SELF_BEST the labelled genotype is the best match WARN SELF_LENIENT, UNCLEAR the labelled genotype is not the best, but no other genotype is clearly ahead FAIL SINGLE_NEW_BEST, MULTI_NEW_BEST of a mapped sample one (or a few) other genotypes match clearly better NO_TEST NO_SELF, NO_OBS_TRAITS, every unmapped sample, NOT_SCORED nothing to confirm or reject

NOT_SCORED is anqchor's status for an omics sample missing from qpgen's output, for example a sample without covariates.

A NOT_SCORED sample keeps its assigned genotype ID (from the sample map) in geno_id_assigned, so it is counted as mapped, and summary.json warnings says how many samples were not scored.

Proposed relabel. A mapped FAIL sample gets proposed_geno_id = its best genotype when Z(1) − Z(2) ≥ z_diff, unless that genotype is the confirmed (PASS) match of another omics sample. Relabelling would then map two samples to one genotype, so proposed_geno_id stays empty and the note says "no relabel proposed: best genotype is the confirmed match of another sample". The sample is still a mismatch.

Rescue candidates. An unmapped sample with SINGLE_NEW_BEST stays NO_TEST (there is no label to confirm) and is listed in candidates.tsv with its best genotype, unless that genotype is the confirmed match of another sample (the same rule as above; the report shows such a sample as "ID already used").

Two genotype IDs (duplicates). A sample matches two genotype IDs about equally when its top two candidates stand clear of the third by more than z_diff (qpgen's MULTI_NEW_BEST test at k = 2), the second scores above z_threshold, and the second scores at least 0.8 × the first. The two genotypes then most likely come from one person: a genotype sample listed twice, or identical twins. Relatives do not qualify: a first-degree relative scores about half the self Z (0.51–0.74 of it on the example data, for samples whose own score is strong), a duplicated genotype 1.00 (0.90 with 2% of its calls changed). A duplicate whose second score does not stand clear of the background cannot be told from noise and is not flagged. The flag does not change qpgen_status or group; such samples are listed in duplicates.tsv and named in the verdict. When the assigned ID is one of the two (or no ID is assigned), the sample is not a mismatch: it gets no proposed_geno_id, is not a rescue candidate, and is left out of the verdict's mismatches, n_fail, failing and swaps.tsv (n_fail_two_ids counts such FAILs). Duplicates alone make the verdict a warning. With a small z_diff (1 on the example data) a near-tie at background level can qualify too.

Swaps. A pair A, B where A's best genotype is B's label and B's best is A's is listed as reciprocal when at least one side is a clear mismatch (SINGLE_NEW_BEST, a FAIL), and as reciprocal-weak otherwise (for example two SELF_LENIENT samples whose own genotype is second by a hair). Only reciprocal pairs count in n_reciprocal_swaps. Every other FAIL sample is listed as one-way, with the sample (if any) that holds its best genotype as partner.

Possible relatives. A sample is flagged when its top five start with a block of k = 2..4 candidates, the best included, that stands out: the largest drop Z(k) − Z(k+1) (k = 2..4) is at least 1.0 and Z(k) ≥ z_threshold. A first-degree relative's Z is roughly half the self Z, and the best unrelated individuals reach Z ≈ 3 (on the example data the median third-best Z is 2.7), so neither "within z_diff of the best" nor a Z threshold alone describes a relative; the drop to the background does. The flag is informational and does not change the group. A sample that matches two genotype IDs about equally is listed in duplicates.tsv instead. The report does not show relatives.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
Everything is under the run directory; per-dataset files under match/<ds>/. Full schemas are in Output files.

File Content match/<ds>/samples.tsv one row per omics sample: status, group, Z-scores, top five, proposal and note match/<ds>/swaps.tsv swaps: kind = reciprocal, reciprocal-weak (not counted) or one-way match/<ds>/candidates.tsv rescue candidates (unmapped samples with one clearly leading genotype) match/<ds>/duplicates.tsv samples that match two genotype IDs about equally match/<ds>/related.tsv samples whose top candidates start with a block of possible relatives match/<ds>/weights.tsv per-trait weight with the reference trait and a weight_le0 flag match/<ds>/summary.json counts per status and group, verdict, failing samples, weight quantiles, parameters match/<ds>/qpgen.weights.tsv.gz, qpgen.match.assigned.tsv.gz, qpgen.match.all.tsv.gz qpgen's own outputs, unchanged match/<ds>/qpgen.params.json resolved parameters: argv, λ mode and value, trait and sample counts, warnings, log excerpt match/<ds>/trait_map.used.tsv the trait pairs used (traits with both a PRS and an omics column) prs/<ref>/prs.prs.tsv.gz, prs.se.tsv.gz PRS of every genotyped individual (regenie layout) report/match.html the report, written by match report or match all anqchor.resolved.yaml, run.json, logs/<step>.log settings, provenance, one log per step

docs.title: samples.tsv
docs.text: Column Meaning pheno_id omics sample ID geno_id_assigned labelled genotype (from the sample map, or the identical ID; empty when unmapped); kept for NOT_SCORED samples qpgen_status status as above (NOT_SCORED if qpgen did not score the sample) group PASS, WARN, FAIL, NO_TEST z_self, cor_self, rank_self Z-score, weighted correlation and rank of the labelled genotype n_traits traits observed for the sample best_id, z_best, cor_best best-matching genotype second_id, z_second, z_gap second-best genotype and z_best − z_second proposed_geno_id best genotype for a FAIL with a clear gap; empty otherwise, and empty when that genotype is another sample's confirmed match note who holds the best genotype, why no relabel is proposed, rescue candidate, two genotype IDs, several leading genotypes, possible relatives id_1…id_5, z_1…z_5 the top five candidates

docs.title: The other tables
docs.text: File Columns swaps.tsv kind pheno_id geno_id_assigned group best_id z_best z_self rank_self partner_pheno_id partner_geno_id_assigned partner_group partner_best_id candidates.tsv pheno_id candidate_geno_id z_best second_id z_second z_gap n_traits candidate_assigned_to duplicates.tsv pheno_id geno_id_assigned group geno_id_1 z_1 geno_id_2 z_2 z_3 assigned_in_pair related.tsv pheno_id geno_id_assigned group n_close close_ids close_z assigned_in_close weights.tsv trait ref_trait weight n_obs weight_le0 (weight = correlation of PRS and trait over mapped samples)

docs.title: summary.json
docs.text: The main keys: verdict (one sentence) and verdict_status (good, warning, or critical when any sample fails); status_counts and group_counts; failing (each FAIL with Z-scores, proposal and note, except samples that match two genotype IDs, one of them their own); n_fail (the same samples) and n_fail_two_ids; n_reciprocal_swaps, n_rescue_candidates, n_duplicates, n_related; n_pheno, n_scored, n_not_scored, n_mapped, n_unmapped, n_prs_samples; n_traits_used, n_traits_weight_le0 and weights (quantiles); the parameters (use_cov, rint, mahalanobis, lambda_mode, lambda_used, z_threshold, z_diff); warnings; qpgen_argv; and n_status_disagreements, which is 0 unless the qpgen build applies different status rules from anqchor's port.

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
report/match.html is a single file that works offline. Its title is "Sample identity matching with anQChor". From top to bottom:

  1. Header: counts (omics samples, genotypes, traits) and the scoring used; with independent scoring, a short tip to try --mahalanobis.
  2. Dashboard: tiles (number first) for samples with an assigned ID, strict match to own ID (SELF_BEST), lenient match to own ID (SELF_BEST + SELF_LENIENT), matches another sample (SINGLE_NEW_BEST), matches two genotype IDs (every sample in Duplicates), matches several (MULTI_NEW_BEST), own ID too weak (UNCLEAR) and not scored (NO_OBS_TRAITS, NOT_SCORED); the two-IDs, several and not-scored tiles appear only when non-zero. A "No assigned ID" tile appears when some samples have no ID; its line splits them into new ID found, ID already used, two genotype IDs, no clear match and not scored. Tiles, cards, chart legend, table filters and table use the same result names. Clicking a tile filters the sample table.
  3. Sliders for the lenient cutoff (z_threshold) and the clear lead (z_diff), each with a one-line hint (no info icons), and one line explaining the match score. Every count, card, chart point, duplicate and table row is reclassified in the browser with qpgen's rules. Copy as config gives the YAML lines that make the values permanent; the files in the run directory keep the values of the run.
  4. Samples to check: one card per sample with an assigned ID that is not a strict match, per sample that matches two genotype IDs, and per sample without an assigned ID. When more than six samples have no ID, one card summarises them instead (counts per result, and how many with no clear match have a best genotype that no other sample uses). Two or more samples not scored share one card. An own-ID-too-weak card names the best genotype, its lead and the lead needed, and whether that genotype matches its own sample.
  5. How clearly each sample matches one genotype: every scored sample, assigned or not, by its best match score (across) and its runner-up score (up). Below the dashed line the best genotype leads by more than the clear lead (grey shade, "one genotype clearly best"; a mismatch can lie there too); on the dotted diagonal the two tie. Samples without an assigned ID are hollow markers. The report calls qpgen's Z-score the "match score".
  6. Duplicates: samples that match two genotype IDs about equally (see the rule above), with the two scores and the next one. A compact line says when there are none. Mismatches and relatives are not listed here.
  7. All samples: searchable, sortable table (the page scrolls; the header stays on screen), 500 rows per page by default (100 on phones), with a TSV download of the current view. Columns (short one-line headers, fixed widths): sample, result, own score, own rank, best other (ID), its score, lead (own score minus the best other score; negative when another genotype fits better, red only for mismatches; for samples without an assigned ID, the best genotype's lead over the next, in italics) and suggested ID; an "Assigned ID" column appears when some assigned IDs differ from the sample IDs. On phones the table shows sample (with the best other genotype under it), result, own score and lead.
  8. Run details (collapsed): settings, the trait-weight histogram, the report's result names with their qpgen_status codes, the qpgen command and a log excerpt.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
• FAIL with a proposed_geno_id and a reciprocal partner: a sample swap; relabel both. A reciprocal-weak pair is not evidence of a swap on its own.
  • One-way FAIL whose best genotype belongs to a PASS sample: a mismatch; no relabel is proposed because that individual already has a matching omics sample. Exclude the sample or check the lab records.
  • A sample in duplicates.tsv: its two leading genotypes are probably one person under two genotype IDs (a duplicated genotype sample or identical twins). When the own ID is one of the two, the omics label is fine: check the genotype set. qpgen calls it MULTI_NEW_BEST (or SELF_BEST when the own ID ranks first by a hair).
  • One-way FAIL with a proposed_geno_id: the sample probably comes from that individual, who has no confirmed omics sample of their own; relabel after checking.
  • Other MULTI_NEW_BEST: several leading genotypes, possibly a mixed sample or a block of close relatives.
  • WARN (SELF_LENIENT): the own genotype is close to the best. With few informative traits this is noise; a larger reference separates better.
  • Many UNCLEAR samples or low Z overall: too few or weak reference traits, a wrong trait map, or phenotypes in another orientation.

After match

cis and trans require identical sample IDs in genotypes and phenotypes and do not read the match results. Rename or drop samples in your input files before running them.

docs.title: Example data
docs.text:
On the shipped MAGE chromosome 21/22 example (729 samples × 367 genes, 729 genotyped individuals, known eQTLs from GTEx), with the defaults:

Group Count Statuses PASS 713 SELF_BEST WARN 16 14 SELF_LENIENT; 2 UNCLEAR: NA11919 (own Z 0.41, rank 253; best HG00237 at 3.60 leads the next by only 0.32) and NA12717 (own Z 1.94, rank 13; every candidate at background level) FAIL 0 NO_TEST 0

All 367 traits are used, 14 with weight ≤ 0 (median 0.24, range −0.35 to 0.80), and 8 samples are flagged as possibly related. The use case explains these results and how they change with the thresholds and scoring options.

docs.title: trans: replication, hotspots and inflation
docs.text:
Question: if I run a trans-xQTL scan (variants against genes far away) with a given setup, does it recover the known signals, does it report hotspots, and are its p-values calibrated? And which of several setups does best?

A setup is one set of inputs: genotypes, phenotypes, covariates, the phenotype transform (as given, or RINT with --rint) and the reference pairs. You evaluate each setup in its own run, compare the runs, and read one report.

A worked example on the MAGE data, with every number explained: Use case: trans evaluation.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  A["trans run<br/>setup A"] --> C["trans compare"]
  B["trans run<br/>setup B"] --> C
  D["trans run<br/>setup C"] --> C
  C --> T["comparison tables"]
  C --> H["report/trans.html"]
Command What it does HTML anqchor trans run tests the rectangle for one setup and writes the summary tables of that run no anqchor trans compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR compares any finished runs, writes comparison tables yes (--no-report to skip) anqchor trans report --out DIR re-renders report/trans.html of a comparison or of a single run from its tables (about 1 s, never runs qpgen) yes anqchor trans all trans run and then trans report on the same run directory (one run, no comparison) yes

Each run tests a rectangle: every variant of the reference pairs against every gene of the reference pairs, with qpgentools rect-assoc. Each test is a cell of the rectangle. From the cells, a run reports three things:

  1. Replicated reference pairs, cis and trans separately: do the known pairs come back with the same sign and a small p-value?
  2. Hotspots: genomic bins (1 Mb by default) whose variants seem to affect many genes far away. A few real hotspots exist; many hotspots usually mean a confounder.
  3. Inflation: the cells whose variant and gene are on different chromosomes should be almost all null. λ_GC, observed vs expected counts and a QQ plot show whether they are.

docs.title: Evaluate several setups
docs.text:
Run one trans run per setup, each into its own directory, then compare the runs. The commands below use the example data shipped in the repository and run from its root:

D=examples/mage/data
IN=(--geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv
    --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz
    --trait-annot $D/pheno/mage_genes.chr21_22.bed
    --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz)
COV=(--cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz)

anqchor trans run "${IN[@]}"                                              --out results/trans/nocov
anqchor trans run "${IN[@]}" "${COV[@]}" --cov-include sex,PC1-5          --out results/trans/basic
anqchor trans run "${IN[@]}" "${COV[@]}" --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 --out results/trans/peer10
anqchor trans run "${IN[@]}" "${COV[@]}"                                  --out results/trans/peer60
anqchor trans run "${IN[@]}" "${COV[@]}" --rint                           --out results/trans/peer60_rint

anqchor trans compare results/trans/nocov results/trans/basic results/trans/peer10 \
    results/trans/peer60 results/trans/peer60_rint --out results/trans/compare

(IN and COV are shell arrays, so the commands work in both bash and zsh.) Each run takes about 8 s on the example data (346 variants × 367 genes); the runs are independent and can run at the same time. trans compare takes about 1 s, runs no association test and writes results/trans/compare/report/trans.html. To re-render that page later (for example after updating anqchor), without running anything else:

anqchor trans report --out results/trans/compare

trans report --out RUN_DIR renders the page of a single run in the same way.

Flag Meaning --geno-list or --pfile genotypes: a qpgen pgen list, or one PLINK2 prefix --pheno, --pheno-format phenotype matrix (default format regenie) --trait-annot gene loci (BED-like chrom start end id, start = TSS); needed to tell cis from trans --trait-id-rule how reference trait IDs map onto phenotype columns (default as_is; e.g. strip_version for versioned ENSG IDs) --pairs reference pairs trait variant beta se [pval]: their variants and genes make the rectangle, and they are the pairs to replicate --cov, --cov-format covariates; omit --cov for none --cov-include only these covariates of --cov (comma-separated; PEER1-10 expands) --cat-cov-names categorical covariates coded as numbers (non-numeric columns such as sex are categorical automatically) --rint RINT of the phenotypes after covariate adjustment (rect-assoc --rint-after-adj). Default: the phenotypes as given --cis-window-bp cis window around the gene start (default 1,000,000) --hotspot-bin-bp bin width for hotspots (default 1,000,000) --hotspot-min-traits genes a bin needs to be a hotspot (default 5; the report can change it) --variants, --traits other variants (a CHROM:POS:REF:ALT list) or genes (all, or a file) for the rectangle --min-maf minimum minor allele frequency (default 0.01) --dataset-name, --reference-name names of the dataset and the reference in the run's files (default dataset, reference) -j, --jobs steps run at the same time (default 1)

trans compare takes the run directories and:

Flag Meaning -o, --out (required) the comparison directory to write --label a label per run, in order (repeat once per run). Default: the run directory names, or <parent>_<name> when two names are the same --report/--no-report also write report/trans.html (default) or the tables only --plotlyjs embed (default, works offline) or cdn

A run tests one phenotype transform. Phenotypes are often already inverse-normal transformed; to see what RINT changes, make a second run with --rint and compare.

With flags only, the dataset is called dataset, the reference reference and the run's covariate set default, so a run's tables are under trans/dataset/. A run can also be written as a configuration file (examples/mage/trans.yaml, the all-covariate run), which is also how to set what has no flag (levels, trait_chroms, known_pairs, max_sig_rows); see Configuration.

Every run directory holds anqchor.resolved.yaml (all settings, flags included) and run.json (provenance). --config RUN/anqchor.resolved.yaml --out NEW reproduces a run; a comparison keeps a copy of each run's settings in settings/<label>.anqchor.yaml. Running the same trans run again does nothing; a changed setting re-runs only what depends on it: --hotspot-min-traits 2 or --hotspot-bin-bp 500000 re-runs only the summary (about 2 s). --out of trans compare must be a new directory or an earlier trans comparison (which is replaced); a run directory or a cis comparison is refused.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
cis and trans. A (variant, gene) pair is cis when the variant is on the gene's chromosome within --cis-window-bp (1 Mb) of the gene start (TSS); every other pair whose gene has a locus is trans: on another chromosome (cross-chromosome), or on the same chromosome farther than the window. Genes without a locus are counted apart. The same rule classifies the cells of the rectangle and the reference pairs.

Replication. A tested reference pair replicates at a level when its effect has the reference's sign and, for the p-value levels, p < 0.05 or p < 1e-5 (the levels of the cis report). Pairs whose variant is not in the genotypes, or that have no result, are counted as not tested.

Hotspots. Trans cells only. Variants are grouped into bins of --hotspot-bin-bp by position (bin = ⌊position / bin width⌋ on each chromosome). A bin's count at a p-value threshold is the number of distinct genes with a trans cell below the threshold from any variant of the bin, not counting genes in cis with the bin (gene start within the cis window of any tested variant of the bin), so the tail of a cis signal is not counted as a trans signal. A hotspot is a bin with at least k genes. The summary holds the hotspot count for every threshold among p < 1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6, 5e-8, 1e-8 and 1e-10, the configured levels (levels.nominal 1e-5, optional levels.strict) and Bonferroni (0.05 / trans cells tested), and every k among 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20 and --hotspot-min-traits. The report opens on p < levels.nominal (1e-5) and k = --hotspot-min-traits. With k = 1 the count is the number of bins with any trans signal.

Inflation. The cross-chromosome cells. When the reference has trans pairs, the cells of every variant within the cis window of a reference trans pair's variant, and every cell of that pair's gene, are left out, so that known trans signals do not count as inflation; the summary says how many cells were left out. Then:

  • λ_GC = median χ²(1) statistic of the cells / 0.4549 (the χ²(1) median); 1 when calibrated. anqchor warns above 1.1 and below 1/1.1.
  • Observed vs expected cells at p < 1e-3 and p < 1e-5 (expected = cells × p).
  • QQ plot: observed against expected −log10 p, with the 95% range of each order statistic under no association (rank r of n uniform p-values follows Beta(r, n − r + 1)).

All of these are computed exactly from qpgen's output in one streaming pass.

docs.title: Steps of a run
docs.text:
With flags only, the dataset is called dataset and the run's single strategy default (--dataset-name changes the first). Step names below use <ds> and <s> for them.

Step What it does prepare.* input preparation (the trait mapping is skipped for a variants-only reference) trans.<ds>.lists variants.txt (sorted, de-duplicated, genotype chromosome style), traits.txt (after trait_chroms), lists.json trans.<ds>.<s>.inputs the run's covariates and strategy.json trans.<ds>.<s>.rect.<t> qpgentools rect-assoc; <t> is raw, or rint with --rint trans.<ds>.summarize streams the rectangle: replication by class, hotspot bins and grid, inflation report.trans report/trans.html; only with trans all or trans report

The qpgen command of the peer10 run (from the run's Makefile):

qpgentools rect-assoc --pgen-list prepare/genotypes/pgen_list.tsv \
    --pheno prepare/datasets/dataset/pheno.regenie.tsv.gz --var-list trans/dataset/variants.txt \
    --out trans/dataset/strategies/default/rect_assoc.raw.tsv.gz \
    --cov trans/dataset/strategies/default/cov.regenie.tsv.gz --pheno-list trans/dataset/traits.txt \
    --cat-cov-names sex --min-maf 0.01 --min-mac 1 --max-chunk-vars 100

--pheno-list is omitted only with traits: all and trait_chroms: all; --rint adds --rint-after-adj. --cat-cov-names lists the categorical covariates among the run's covariates; it is left out without covariates or when none is categorical.

Memory. The summarizer streams the wide matrix in row chunks and keeps the −log10 p of the cross-chromosome cells used for inflation as float32 (4 bytes per cell, plus a sorted copy), per-variant counts, and the cells below the loosest hotspot threshold with their effects.

docs.title: The rectangle
docs.text:
Flag (config key) Value Effect --variants (variants) reference (default) the reference's variants present in the genotypes file one CHROM:POS:REF:ALT per line --traits (traits) reference (default) the genes of the reference pairs all every gene of the phenotype file file gene IDs in the first column config only (trait_chroms) genotyped (default) keep genes whose locus is on a genotyped chromosome all no restriction (genes without a locus are kept too) list e.g. [21, 22], either chromosome style

With a pair file that holds cis and trans eQTLs, the rectangle contains both kinds of signal. With a cis-only pair file (as in the example), every reference pair is cis and the trans side of the report says so.

docs.title: Outputs of a run
docs.text:
Under each run directory (column schemas: Output files):

File Content trans/<ds>/summary.json the run, cell counts per class, replication by class, the hotspot grid, inflation, definitions, warnings trans/<ds>/reference_pairs.tsv every reference pair: class, status, effect, z, −log10 p, replication flags trans/<ds>/hotspots.tsv one row per bin with a tested variant: genes with a trans signal at each grid threshold, strongest cell trans/<ds>/hotspot_genes.tsv one row per bin and gene with a trans signal at the loosest grid threshold trans/<ds>/qq.tsv QQ quantiles of the cross-chromosome cells with the 95% band trans/<ds>/variants.tsv per variant: cells by class, trans signals, strongest trans and cis gene, left out of inflation or not trans/<ds>/pairs.sig.tsv.gz every cell with p < levels.nominal (1e-5), any class (at most max_sig_rows) trans/<ds>/variants.txt, traits.txt, lists.json the rectangle trans/<ds>/strategies/default/rect_assoc.{raw,rint}.tsv.gz qpgen output report/trans.html the page of this run alone (trans all / trans report) anqchor.resolved.yaml, run.json settings and provenance

Rows are labelled (run column) with the run directory name.

docs.title: Outputs of a comparison
docs.text:
anqchor trans compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR reads finished runs (never qpgen). Each run gets a label: the run directory name (<parent>_<name> when two are the same), or the --label values in order. The comparison directory holds (column schemas):

File Content runs.tsv one row per run: the inputs (genotypes, phenotypes, covariates, rint, reference), the rectangle and its cells, replicated reference pairs per class (cis_*, trans_*, and *_common over the pairs tested in every run), λ_GC, observed and expected counts, the hotspot count at the run's opening threshold and minimum (n_hotspots) and at the first run's (n_hotspots_shared, the same setting for every run) hotspot_grid.tsv hotspot counts per run, threshold and minimum genes hotspots.tsv, hotspot_genes.tsv, qq.tsv, reference_pairs.tsv the runs' tables stacked, with a run column summary.json the runs, the comparability checks, each run's summary and the warnings compare.json manifest (runs, labels, command); trans report uses it to recognise a comparison directory settings/<label>.anqchor.yaml the exact settings of each compared run report/trans.html the report (unless --no-report)

Comparability. λ_GC, the observed counts and the hotspots are statistics of each run's whole rectangle, so they compare directly only when the runs tested the same cells. anqchor checks that the runs used the same genotype samples, phenotype samples, reference, rectangle, cell counts, cis window, bin width and opening hotspot setting, and prints a warning for each difference (for example "the runs tested different variant–gene tests (…)"). Reference pairs are matched across runs by gene and variant; the *_common columns count only the pairs tested in every run, and the report uses them when the runs tested different pairs and share at least one.

docs.title: Reading the report
docs.text:
Title Comparing N runs: trans-QTL evaluation with anQChor (a single run: trans-QTL evaluation with anQChor). Under it, one line with the number of runs, the rectangle, the cross-chromosome cells, the samples and the reference file, then any warning. Runs keep one color everywhere on the page. Then:

  1. Replicated reference pairs. Two blocks, cis and trans; in each, one row per run with the pairs of the same sign, with p < 0.05 and with p < 1e-5, as counts, percentages of the tested pairs and bars (only the pairs tested in every run when the runs tested different pairs). "No trans pairs in the reference" when there are none.
  2. Hotspots. Two rows of buttons choose the p-value threshold and the minimum genes per bin; the choice applies to every run. One row per run gives its number of hotspots and a bar for the share of bins that are hotspots. Below, for one run at a time (buttons, or a list with more than five runs or long labels; clicking a run's row also selects it): the genes with a trans signal per bin along the genome (hotspots in the run's color, the minimum dotted; hover a bar for its genes), the grid of hotspot counts over every threshold and minimum (click a cell to apply it to every run), and the top 10 hotspot bins with their genes ("Show all" for the rest).
  3. Inflation. λ_GC per run (a dot per run, dotted line at 1), the QQ plot with one line per run over the grey 95% band (Zoom, the default, cuts the y axis at 1.5 times the band and names the runs above it; Full shows everything), and observed vs expected counts at p < 1e-3 and p < 1e-5 per run, with the ratio when at least 5 are expected or 10 observed (red when it is more than twice the expected).
  4. Run details (collapsed): per run the covariates, rank normalization, samples, rectangle, tests, Bonferroni threshold, bin width and a link to its saved settings; the definitions; every reference pair with −log10 p per run (negative: opposite sign; sorted by the first run); links to the tables.

The page of a single run shows the same three items for that run: cis and trans as rows, the number of hotspots in large type, and the QQ plot with λ_GC and the observed counts beside it.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
• Calibrate first. λ_GC near 1 and QQ lines inside the band mean calibrated tests. Well above 1 means missing covariates, population structure or batch effects: every significant trans cell of that run is then suspect, and hotspots appear everywhere.
  • Hotspots that disappear with covariates were artefacts. Hotspots that remain with good covariates and recur across thresholds are worth a look; if many bins hit the same few genes, suspect a shared confounder before biology.
  • Strong trans hits that survive good covariates are often paralogs or duplicated regions (reads or variant calls mapped to the wrong copy). Check the gene names.
  • cis replication says the setup recovers known local signals; trans replication needs a reference with trans pairs and is usually much lower, because trans effects are small.
  • Choose the run that keeps λ_GC near 1, has no hotspots it cannot explain, and replicates the most pairs at p < 1e-5.
  • The more cells the rectangle has, the stricter the threshold has to be: read the hotspot grid at Bonferroni as well as at the fixed thresholds.

docs.text:
On the example data (346 GTEx variants × 367 genes on chr21/22; 126,982 cells: 6,186 cis, 53,508 cross-chromosome, 67,288 same chromosome beyond 1 Mb). The GTEx reference has only cis pairs, so nothing is left out of the inflation cells. Details in the use case.
