docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Generated from anqchor <command> --help (version 0.1.0.dev0). Run any command with --help for the same information. Commands are shown as run from the repository root.

anqchor [--version] [-v/--verbose] [--qpgen PATH] COMMAND [ARGS]...
Root option Meaning --version show the version and exit -v, --verbose debug logging --qpgen PATH path to qpgentools (overrides discovery and qpgen.binary) Command Purpose match run, match report, match all sample identity matching cis run, cis compare, cis report, cis all replication of known cis pairs, and comparison of runs trans run, trans compare, trans report, trans all trans evaluation: replicated reference pairs, hotspots, inflation steps list the steps of a run with their status run, report several analyses from one configuration file qpgen build, qpgen check build and check qpgen prepare index-pvar, pgen-list, pheno, cov standalone input utilities

docs.title: Common run options
docs.text:
Shared by match run|all, cis run|all, trans run|all and the top-level run.

Option Meaning -c, --config FILE YAML configuration file (optional when the input flags are given) -o, --out PATH run directory (overrides out_dir) -j, --jobs INT steps to run in parallel (make -j); default 1 --threads INT threads for qpgentools match-prs-pheno (qpgen.threads), which only identity matching runs; cis and trans use single-threaded qpgen commands. Changing it re-runs nothing --dataset NAME restrict to this dataset of a multi-dataset configuration (repeatable) --strategy NAME restrict to this strategy of a configuration file (repeatable; cis, trans and run only) --dry-run write the Makefile, show what would run, run nothing; an existing anqchor.resolved.yaml is left unchanged (it is written only when the directory has none) --until STEP run up to and including this step --only STEP re-run only this step (its upstream steps must be up to date) --force re-run the selected steps and everything upstream --keep-going continue with independent steps after a failure --plotlyjs embed\|cdn report plotly.js: embedded (offline, default) or from a CDN (small files)

docs.title: Input flags
docs.text:
Available on match run|all, cis run|all and trans run|all. Without --config they define all inputs; with --config they override the file (see precedence). Paths are relative to the current directory.

Option Meaning Config key --geno-list FILE qpgen pgen list (CHROM BEG END PREFIX) genotypes.pgen_list --pfile PREFIX single PLINK2 prefix with .pgen/.psam/.pvar.idx.gz genotypes.pfile --pheno FILE phenotype matrix datasets.<name>.pheno --pheno-format FMT regenie (default), tensorqtl, tsv-sample-row, tsv-sample-col datasets.<name>.pheno_format --cov FILE covariate matrix datasets.<name>.cov --cov-format FMT layout of --cov datasets.<name>.cov_format --cat-cov-names NAMES comma-separated categorical covariates of --cov (e.g. sex,batch); their text levels are encoded by qpgen. Non-numeric covariate columns are treated as categorical automatically, so the flag is needed only for categories coded as numbers datasets.<name>.cov_categorical --trait-annot FILE trait loci, BED-like or tensorQTL matrix (cis, trans) datasets.<name>.trait_annot --trait-id-rule RULE as_is, before_colon, strip_version, before_colon_strip_version datasets.<name>.trait_id_rule --sample-map FILE geno_id pheno_id map (match only) datasets.<name>.sample_map --pairs FILE reference pairs, columns trait variant beta se, and pval when present references.<name>.pairs --dataset-name NAME dataset name for these flags (default dataset) --reference-name NAME reference name for these flags (default reference)

docs.title: anqchor match run
docs.text:
Run sample identity matching up to the summary tables (pair-prs, match-prs-pheno, summaries). No HTML; render it with anqchor match report --out DIR.

anqchor trans run --geno-list G --pheno P --pairs R --trait-annot T [--cov C [--cov-include NAMES]] [--rint] --out DIR [options]

Common run options, input flags (no --sample-map), and:

Option Config key Meaning --cov-include NAMES pipelines.trans.strategies use only these covariates of --cov: comma-separated names; ranges such as PEER1-10 expand. Default: every covariate in --cov. Omit --cov for no covariates --variants FILE variants (or a trans reference) variant list (CHROM:POS:REF:ALT per line) instead of the reference's variants; without --config and --pairs it defines a variants-only reference --traits reference\|all\|FILE traits rectangle genes (file: prefix optional); default reference --rint / --no-rint pipelines.trans.rint apply a rank-based inverse normal transform to the phenotypes after covariate adjustment (rect-assoc --rint-after-adj). Default: test the phenotypes as given (one transform per run) --cis-window-bp INT cis_window_bp a variant within this distance of a gene's start on the same chromosome is cis (default 1000000); every other pair is trans --min-maf X min_maf minimum minor allele frequency --hotspot-bin-bp INT hotspot_bin_bp bin width that thins trans signals for hotspots (default 1000000) --hotspot-min-traits INT hotspot_min_traits genes with a trans signal that make a bin a hotspot (default 5; the report lets you change it)

To evaluate several covariate sets or RINT, start one trans run per setup, each with its own --out, then compare the runs with trans compare. A configuration file holds one setup too (one entry under pipelines.trans.strategies). trait_chroms, levels and max_sig_rows have no flag. Output files: Output files.

docs.title: anqchor trans compare
docs.text:
Compare finished trans runs (any inputs) and write comparison tables and the HTML report.

anqchor trans compare RUN_DIR [RUN_DIR...] --out DIR [--label L ...] [--no-report] [--plotlyjs embed|cdn]
Argument / option Meaning RUN_DIR... (required) run directories written by anqchor trans run -o, --out PATH (required) comparison directory to write --label STR label for each run, in order (repeat once per run); default: the run directory names (<parent>_<name> when two are the same) --report / --no-report also write report/trans.html (default --report) --plotlyjs embed\|cdn plotly.js embedded or from a CDN

Prints a warning: line per difference between the runs (genotype samples, reference, samples, rectangle, tests, cis window, bin width, opening hotspot setting) and per run warning, then compared N run(s): <labels>, the table directory and the report path. Labels must be distinct; the number of --label values must equal the number of runs, a run directory may appear only once, and --out must be a new directory or an earlier trans comparison (not a run directory or a cis comparison); exit 2 otherwise. Output files: Output files.

docs.title: anqchor trans report
docs.text:
(Re-)render report/trans.html from existing tables. Runs no analysis.

anqchor trans report --out DIR [--plotlyjs embed|cdn]
Option Meaning -o, --out PATH (required) a trans run directory or a trans compare directory --plotlyjs embed\|cdn plotly.js embedded or from a CDN

A cis compare directory is refused (exit 2) with a pointer to cis report, and cis report refuses a trans compare directory the same way.

docs.title: anqchor trans all
docs.text: trans run followed by trans report on the same run directory (one run, no comparison). Same options as trans run.

docs.title: anqchor steps
docs.text:
List the steps of a run with their status (done, stale, missing) and descriptions.

anqchor steps --config FILE [--out PATH] [--pipeline P]... [--dataset D]... [--strategy S]...

--config is required; a run's own anqchor.resolved.yaml works. The command writes the Makefile but runs nothing, and leaves the run's anqchor.resolved.yaml unchanged. It always lists the report step, so after match run, cis run or trans run the report step shows as missing or stale.

docs.title: anqchor run
docs.text:
Run every pipeline enabled in a configuration file, sharing common steps.

anqchor run --config FILE [--pipeline match|cis|trans]... [common run options]

--config is required and input flags are not accepted. -p, --pipeline (repeatable) selects pipelines regardless of enabled. Reports are rendered as part of the run, and report/index.html links them when more than one pipeline runs.

docs.title: anqchor report
docs.text:
Re-render HTML reports of an anqchor run directory from existing summaries; runs missing upstream steps if needed.

anqchor report --config FILE [--out PATH] [--pipeline P]... [--plotlyjs embed|cdn] [--force]

--force re-renders even if up to date. Without --pipeline it renders every pipeline enabled in the file. For a single analysis, anqchor match report --out DIR, anqchor cis report --out DIR and anqchor trans report --out DIR are simpler.

docs.title: anqchor qpgen build
docs.text:
Build qpgentools from the submodule (htslib, qgenlib, then qpgen).

Option Meaning --src PATH qpgen checkout (default: the extern/qpgen submodule) -j, --jobs INT parallel compile jobs (default 4) --force rebuild htslib and qgenlib too --cmake-arg ARG extra argument for cmake (repeatable)

Prints the binary path. Exit 4 on failure, with the tail of extern/qpgen/anqchor-build.log.

docs.title: anqchor qpgen check
docs.text:
Locate qpgentools, verify its subcommands (pair-prs, match-prs-pheno, pair-assoc, rect-assoc), and print its path, discovery source, sha256 and git commit. It does not check the qpgen version; run qpgentools --version (0.2.0 or later is required).

Option Meaning --qpgen PATH binary to check (default: discovery order)

docs.title: anqchor prepare index-pvar
docs.text:
Build PREFIX.pvar.idx.gz (9 columns with a 1-based INDEX) and its tabix index.

Option Meaning --pfile PATH (required) PLINK2 prefix; reads PREFIX.pvar, PREFIX.pvar.zst or PREFIX.pvar.gz --force overwrite an existing PREFIX.pvar.idx.gz

docs.title: anqchor prepare pgen-list
docs.text:
Write a qpgen pgen list (CHROM BEG END PREFIX) with absolute prefixes. With checking (the default), each prefix must have .pgen, .psam, .pvar.idx.gz and .tbi, and CHROM is taken from the first pvar record so it matches the pvar spelling.

Option Meaning --prefix-template STR (required) prefix with {chrom}, e.g. geno/chr{chrom} --chroms STR (required) chromosomes, e.g. 1-22,X --out PATH (required) output pgen list --no-check do not check that the files exist

docs.title: anqchor prepare pheno
docs.text:
Convert a phenotype matrix to regenie layout (FID IID trait…).

Option Meaning --in FILE (required) input matrix --format FMT (required) regenie, tensorqtl, tsv-sample-row, tsv-sample-col --out PATH (required) output regenie matrix (.tsv.gz) --missing-str STR string meaning "missing" (repeatable; default NA)

docs.title: anqchor prepare cov
docs.text:
Convert covariates to regenie layout: validate values, drop constant columns, handle missing values. Categorical covariates keep their text levels by default; the command prints the --cat-cov-names value to pass to qpgen with the file.

Option Meaning --in FILE (required) input covariate matrix --format FMT (required) layout --out PATH (required) output regenie covariates (.tsv.gz) --categorical NAME covariate to treat as categorical (repeatable) --missing error\|drop_samples\|impute_mean missing-value policy (default error) --missing-str STR string meaning "missing" (repeatable; default NA) --json PATH also write the encoding summary as JSON --encode / --keep-categorical write categorical covariates as numeric indicator columns (--encode) instead of their text levels (default --keep-categorical; qpgen encodes them with --cat-cov-names) 
anqchor prepare cov --in examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --format regenie --out results/cov.regenie.tsv.gz

wrote results/cov.regenie.tsv.gz: 729 samples x 66 covariates; categorical: sex ['XX', 'XY']
categorical covariates keep their text levels; use --cat-cov-names sex

With --encode, sex is written as one column coded 1 (XX) / 2 (XY), and a covariate with k > 2 levels as k − 1 indicator columns <name>_<level> coded 2 (has the level) or 1; the first sorted level is the reference. Both forms give the same association results.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: 0 success · 2 configuration/validation error (or run directory locked by another command) · 3 a step failed · 4 qpgen missing or unusable. See Running.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Every file a fresh run writes, with its columns or keys. The lists below were taken from runs of match run + match report, cis run (five runs) + cis compare, and trans run (five runs) + trans compare on the example data. Paths are relative to the run (or comparison) directory; file names come from one place, anqchor.pipelines.layout.Layout. Conventions:

  • TSV files have a header (except the plain ID lists and maps noted below), use NA for missing values and 1/0 for booleans; .gz files are gzip/bgzip compressed.
  • Every JSON file has schema_version (currently 1; 3 for the cis summary.json of a run or comparison, which a comparison requires of every run; 2 for the trans summary.json of a run or comparison, which trans compare and trans report require).
  • Paths inside summaries are relative to the run directory.
  • In a flags-only run the dataset is called dataset and the reference reference, so <ds> = dataset and <ref> = reference below.

docs.title: Run-level files
docs.text: File Content anqchor.resolved.yaml complete settings of the last command that ran steps in the directory (defaults filled in, paths absolute, flags included; a dry run or anqchor steps leaves it unchanged); a valid --config file run.json provenance; see Running Makefile generated; rewritten on every invocation .anqchor.lock run-directory lock held while a command runs (a second command on the same directory exits with code 2) steps/<step>.json step signature: name kind pipeline inputs outputs commands params, plus params.qpgen_sha256 for steps that run qpgen and anqchor_version for Python steps steps/<step>.done, .seconds stamp and wall time of the last successful run logs/<step>.log step stdout and stderr

docs.title: cis run
docs.text:
Under cis/<ds>/. A flags-only run has one strategy, default (so <s> = default), and its rows are labelled with the run label, the name of the run directory (run and label columns). A configuration file listing several strategies labels them by strategy name. A run tests one phenotype transform: as given, or RINT with --rint (pipelines.cis.rint).

File Content strategies/<s>/cov.regenie.tsv.gz the run's covariates, regenie layout, categorical covariates as text levels (absent without covariates) strategies/<s>/pheno.regenie.tsv.gz strategy phenotypes (only with a pheno override in a config file) strategies/<s>/strategy.json pipeline dataset strategy cov_source cov_columns n_cov [cat_cov_names cov_include cov_empty cov_file cov_encoding] pheno; cov_columns are the covariate names in the file, n_cov counts the numeric columns after encoding (degrees of freedom), cat_cov_names the categorical covariates passed to qpgen as --cat-cov-names (absent without covariates) strategies/<s>/pair_assoc.tsv.gz pair-assoc output (pair engine): TRAIT CHROM GENPOS ID ALLELE0 ALLELE1 A1FREQ N N_RR N_RA N_AA INFO BETA SE TSTAT LOG10P, plus BETA_RINT SE_RINT TSTAT_RINT LOG10P_RINT with --rint strategies/<s>/rect_assoc.<t>.tsv.gz rect-assoc output (rect engine); <t> = raw, or rint with --rint pairs.long.tsv.gz one row per mapped pair, see below strategies.tsv one row per run, see below traits.tsv trait ref_trait n_pairs n_variant_absent, per run label: best_log10p:<run>, level:<run> (strongest level reached, in level_order), then delta_log10p:<run> (vs the first run; only when there is more than one), and best_run power_curve.tsv run threshold_log10p n_tested n_replicated frac_replicated (sign-concordant with p < 10^−threshold, as the levels; thresholds 0, 0.5, 1, …) summary.json see below

Also report/cis.html after cis report or cis all.

pairs.long.tsv.gz, one row per (run, mapped pair):

Column Meaning run the run label trait, ref_trait, variant dataset trait ID, reference trait ID, CPRA beta_ref, se_ref reference effect (ALT allele) and standard error z_ref reference z-score: beta_ref / se_ref, or, without se_ref, the signed normal quantile of pval_ref pval_ref, log10p_ref the reference's pval column (or the column named by columns.pval) and its −log10, read from the text so that p-values below the double range (1e-400) keep their size; without a usable p-value, log10p_ref is the two-sided normal p-value of z_ref status tested, variant_absent, not_tested (no association row, or no finite statistic) a1freq, n, beta, se, tstat, log10p study statistics (ALT allele, the same allele as beta_ref); RINT statistics with --rint z signed study z-score beta / se (as z_ref); without a usable se, the normal quantile of the two-sided p-value with the sign of beta sign_concordant 1/0, NA when not tested rep_<level> 1/0 for each configured level (sign nominal fdr bonferroni strict)

strategies.tsv, one row per run: run label rint (1 with RINT) n_cov n_pairs n_tested n_variant_absent n_not_tested n_rep_<level>… frac_rep_<level>… median_log10p mean_z2 beta_corr frac_sign_discordant pi1 bonferroni_log10p; with the rect engine also n_control_cells lambda_gc_control n_control_p_lt_1e5 n_control_cross_chrom lambda_gc_control_cross_chrom n_control_cross_chrom_p_lt_1e5; last mean_z2_common (mean z² over the pairs tested in every row's run) and rel_neff = (mean_z2_common − 1) / (first run's mean_z2_common − 1), the effective sample size relative to the first run (1 for a single run).

summary.json keys: schema_version dataset reference engine rint levels (rule per level) level_order (levels from weakest to strongest by their −log10 p cut-off for this run) transform_semantics (as_given, rint, engines, degrees_of_freedom) runs (label strategy rint n_cov per row) baseline n_ref_pairs n_pairs_mapped n_pairs_unmapped n_traits_mapped n_traits_unmapped n_variant_absent n_absent_variants n_absent_variants_indel n_absent_variants_snv absent_variant_examples unresolved_fraction unresolved_by_run max_unresolved_fraction recomputed_log10p per_run (the strategies.tsv numbers by label) ranking (labels per level, best first) recommended (run label key_level reason) warnings sentinels (reserved, null).

docs.title: cis compare
docs.text:
anqchor cis compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR writes into DIR. Each compared run is identified by its label (run = label column); a run whose configuration listed several strategies appears as <label>:<strategy>. Runs may differ in the phenotype transform. A run written by an anqchor version with another cis summary schema is refused with a request to re-run it.

File Content runs.tsv one row per run: label run_dir dataset genotypes n_geno_samples pheno n_pheno_samples n_samples_analysable cov cov_include (all, the names given, or NA) n_cov cov_columns rint reference reference_pairs engine n_pairs_mapped strategies.tsv the columns of a run's strategies.tsv (run = label = run label), plus n_common_tested and n_rep_<level>_common (replication counted only over the pairs tested in every compared run); mean_z2_common and rel_neff are over those pairs, relative to the first run pairs.long.tsv.gz the runs' pairs.long.tsv.gz stacked, run = run label; levels re-derived with the first run's level settings traits.tsv as in a run, one column group per run label; delta_log10p is relative to the first run power_curve.tsv as in a run, per run label summary.json the keys of a run's summary.json (without rint, n_traits_unmapped, recomputed_log10p, unresolved_by_run), plus kind (comparison), runs (the runs.tsv rows) and comparability (same_reference, reference_sha256 per label, rint per label); baseline is the first run's label; warnings include each run's warnings prefixed by its label compare.json manifest: kind (cis), runs (label run_dir dataset settings), labels, argv, cwd settings/<label>.anqchor.yaml a copy of each run's anqchor.resolved.yaml report/cis.html the comparison report (unless --no-report)

docs.text:

<threshold> is p1e-4 p1e-5 p1e-6 p5e-8 p1e-8 p1e-10, the configured levels (e.g. p0.001) and bonferroni; the top cell is the strongest trans cell of the bin among genes not in cis with it (NA without one at the loosest threshold) hotspot_genes.tsv one row per bin and gene with a trans cell below the loosest grid threshold (genes in cis with the bin excluded): chrom bin_start bin_end trait trait_chrom trait_start variant beta se log10p (the strongest variant of the bin for that gene) qq.tsv the cross-chromosome cells used for inflation, at most ~2,000 points (the 250 strongest, then log-spaced ranks): n_cells rank expected_log10p observed_log10p band_lo_log10p band_hi_log10p (95% range of the order statistic, Beta(rank, n − rank + 1)) variants.tsv one row per tested variant: variant chrom pos bin_start a1freq n n_cis n_cross_chrom n_same_chrom_distal n_sig_trans (p < nominal) max_log10p_trans top_trans_trait max_log10p_cis top_cis_trait excluded_from_calibration pairs.sig.tsv.gz every cell with p < levels.nominal (any class), strongest first, at most max_sig_rows: variant chrom pos trait trait_chrom trait_start cell_class (cis/cross_chrom/same_chrom_distal/no_locus) reference_pair distance a1freq n beta se log10p summary.json see below

docs.title: trans compare
docs.text:
anqchor trans compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR writes into DIR. Each compared run is identified by its label (the run directory name or --label; <label>:<ds> for a run with several datasets). A run written by an anqchor version with another trans summary schema is refused with a request to re-run it. Summary schema 2.

then n_variants_tested n_traits_tested n_cells n_cells_cis n_cells_cross_chrom n_cells_same_chrom_distal n_cells_trans cis_window_bp lambda_gc n_inflation_cells n_inflation_cells_excluded observed_p1e-3 expected_p1e-3 observed_p1e-5 expected_p1e-5 hotspot_bin_bp n_bins bonferroni_p hotspot_threshold hotspot_min_genes n_hotspots n_hotspots_shared (n_hotspots: the hotspot count at the run's own opening threshold and minimum; docs.title: report
docs.text:
File Content report/match.html written by match report or match all report/cis.html written by cis report or cis all in a run directory, and by cis compare (or cis report) in a comparison directory report/trans.html written by trans report or trans all in a run directory, and by trans compare (or trans report) in a comparison directory report/index.html only from the top-level anqchor run with more than one pipeline: one tile per pipeline and dataset, with links

Reports are self-contained interactive pages (plotly; every chart has a table view and TSV download); with the default --plotlyjs embed the example reports are 5-10 MB. With --plotlyjs cdn and no network, each chart area shows a notice suggesting --plotlyjs embed. Reports are rendered only from the summaries above, never from qpgen output.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: anqchor is a command-line tool first; the Python modules are documented here for people who extend it. Everything below lives under src/anqchor/.

docs.title: Loading a configuration
docs.text:
from anqchor.config import load_config

cfg = load_config("examples/mage/match.yaml", overrides={"pipelines": {"match": {"z_diff": 2.5}}})
cfg.enabled_pipelines()  # ['match']
cfg.reference_for("match")  # 'gtex_lcl'
cfg.datasets_for("match")  # ['rnaseq']
cfg.pipelines.match.z_diff  # 2.5

load_config merges overrides over the file, validates with the pydantic models in anqchor.config.model, and returns a Config with absolute paths. It raises anqchor.config.load.ConfigError (exit code 2 in the CLI).

docs.title: Layout: file names
docs.text:
anqchor.pipelines.layout.Layout is the single source of truth for every path in a run directory (all relative to it). Producers and consumers must use it instead of formatting paths:

from anqchor.pipelines import Layout

Layout.pgen_list  # prepare/genotypes/pgen_list.tsv
Layout.ds_pheno("rnaseq")  # prepare/datasets/rnaseq/pheno.regenie.tsv.gz
Layout.dsref_pairs("rnaseq", "gtex_lcl")  # prepare/datasets/rnaseq/ref.gtex_lcl/pairs.tsv.gz
Layout.cis_summary("rnaseq", "strategies.tsv")
Layout.rect_assoc("trans", "rnaseq", "peer60", "raw")
Layout.report("cis")  # report/cis.html

docs.title: Step and StepGraph
docs.text:
from anqchor.engine.step import Step

Step(
    name="cis.rnaseq.summarize",  # unique, dotted; also a make target
    kind="summarize_cis",  # registered Python implementation (or None)
    inputs=(...),  # files read (relative to the run directory)
    outputs=(...),  # files written; all must exist after the step
    commands=(),  # shell lines (for qpgen steps)
    params={...},  # JSON-serialisable; part of the signature
    pipeline="cis",
    description="replication of gtex_lcl pairs on rnaseq",
)
  • Steps are linked by paths: when an input of one step is an output of another, the Makefile makes the consumer depend on the producer.
  • params and commands form the step signature (steps/<name>.json). Anything that changes the result must be in them, so that a change re-runs the step and everything downstream.
  • StepGraph de-duplicates identical steps (same name and signature), which is how pipelines share prepare.* and prs.*; a conflicting redefinition or an output produced by two steps is an error.

A pipeline module (anqchor.pipelines.match|cis|trans) exposes build(ctx: BuildContext) -> list[Step] returning its steps plus the shared ones it needs; anqchor.pipelines.build_graph assembles the graph and the make groups; it drops the report.* steps for run commands (reports=False) and adds report.index only when several pipelines run together.

docs.title: Python step implementations
docs.text:
A Python step's command is generated: python -m anqchor _step <name> --run-dir .. The runner reads steps/<name>.json and calls the function registered for its kind:

from anqchor.steps import StepContext, StepError, register
from anqchor.util.files import write_json


@register("my_summary")
def my_summary(ctx: StepContext) -> None:
    ds = ctx.params["dataset"]
    table = ctx.path(ctx.inputs[0])            # absolute path of a declared input
    ...
    if bad:
        raise StepError("actionable message")  # reported without a traceback, exit 3
    write_json(ctx.path(ctx.outputs[0]), {"schema_version": 1, ...})

Rules:

  • Read only declared inputs and params; never read the config file.
  • Write every declared output, atomically (anqchor.util.files.atomic_write, write_json, the write_* helpers in anqchor.io).
  • Turn data problems into StepError (the input_errors decorator in anqchor.steps.prepare converts anqchor.io.InputError).

docs.title: Adding a step kind
docs.text:
1. Implement the function with @register("<kind>") in a module under anqchor/steps/ or anqchor/report/, and make sure the module is listed in anqchor.steps.STEP_MODULES.
  2. Add the output file names to Layout.
  3. Emit the Step from the pipeline's build() with all parameters in params.
  4. Add unit tests with small fixtures (see Development).

docs.title: qpgen command builders and readers
docs.text:
from anqchor.qpgen import commands as qc
from anqchor.qpgen.outputs import read_pair_assoc, iter_rect_assoc

argv = qc.rect_assoc(
    "qpgentools",
    genotypes=qc.Genotypes(pgen_list=Layout.pgen_list),
    pheno="pheno.tsv.gz",
    var_list="variants.txt",
    out="out.tsv.gz",
    min_maf=0.01,
)
qc.to_shell(argv)
for chunk in iter_rect_assoc("out.tsv.gz", ("BETA", "LOG10P")):
    chunk.meta, chunk.stats["LOG10P"]  # rows × traits arrays

anqchor.qpgen.commands is the only module that knows qpgen flag names, and anqchor.qpgen.outputs the only one that knows qpgen output layouts.

docs.title: Comparing cis runs
docs.text:
anqchor cis compare is a thin wrapper around anqchor.steps.cis_compare.compare_runs:

from pathlib import Path
from anqchor.steps.cis_compare import compare_runs, is_comparison_dir

summary = compare_runs(
    [Path("results/cis/nocov"), Path("results/cis/peer10")],
    Path("results/cis/compare"),
    labels=["nocov", "peer10"],
)
summary["recommended"]["label"]  # e.g. 'peer10/rint'
is_comparison_dir(Path("results/cis/compare"))  # True: compare.json exists

It reads each run's anqchor.resolved.yaml and cis/<ds>/ summaries and writes the tables described in Output files; it does not render HTML (the CLI calls anqchor.cli.execute.render_cis_comparison for that). Data problems raise anqchor.steps.StepError.

docs.title: Comparing trans runs
docs.text:
anqchor trans compare wraps anqchor.steps.trans_compare.compare_runs the same way:

from pathlib import Path
from anqchor.steps.compare import comparison_kind
from anqchor.steps.trans_compare import compare_runs

summary = compare_runs(
    [Path("results/trans/nocov"), Path("results/trans/peer10")], Path("results/trans/compare")
)
summary["comparability"]["same_cells"]  # True when the runs tested the same cells
comparison_kind(Path("results/trans/compare"))  # 'trans' (compare.json says so)

It writes the tables described in Output files and no HTML (the CLI calls anqchor.cli.execute.render_trans_comparison).

docs.title: qpgen integration
docs.text: anqchor does no association statistics itself: qpgen (qpgentools) computes polygenic scores, identity scores and association tests. anqchor prepares the inputs, builds the command lines, runs them as steps and reads the outputs. The qpgen flag names appear in one module, anqchor.qpgen.commands; the output layouts in one module, anqchor.qpgen.outputs.

docs.title: Version requirement: qpgen 0.2.0 or later
docs.text:
qpgen is vendored as the git submodule extern/qpgen (branch dev), pinned at commit 5b811e2, which reports version 0.2.0:

$ extern/qpgen/bin/qpgentools --version
qpgentools 0.2.0 (git 5b811e2)

Categorical covariates (--cat-cov-names, below) need a build from commit 5b811e2 or later: cb97eb0 added them to pair-assoc, rect-assoc and region-assoc, and 5b811e2 to match-prs-pheno. Both report version 0.2.0, as does the earlier 76f2fd1, so the version string alone does not tell them apart; an older build does not accept --cat-cov-names. anqchor qpgen check prints the commit of the checkout and fails with missing options: ... when match-prs-pheno, pair-assoc or rect-assoc lacks --cat-cov-names or --max-cat-levels.

Every qpgen command also logs this line first. Builds before 0.2.0 have no --version.

anqchor itself does not read the version: anqchor qpgen check verifies the subcommands and prints the binary's sha256 and the git commit of the checkout it sits in, and run.json records the same. Check qpgentools --version yourself when you use a binary built elsewhere.

docs.title: What changed in qpgen 0.2.0
docs.text:
qpgen 0.2.0 collects the fixes made while anqchor was built and tested on the MAGE example. The ones that change anqchor's results:

Change Effect on older builds pair-assoc adjusts the genotypes for the covariates as well as the phenotype (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell), like rect-assoc with covariates, pair-assoc effects and −log10 p were attenuated and differed from rect-assoc With covariates, pair-assoc, rect-assoc and region-assoc use df = N − 2 − k (k = rank of the covariates) SE too small by √((N−2−k)/(N−2)); −log10 p optimistic with many covariates pair-assoc always fits an intercept; rect-assoc centres phenotypes without covariates without covariates, SE was inflated for phenotypes with a large mean Non-numeric values (such as XX/XY) are an error in every phenotype and covariate loader, except in covariates named with --cat-cov-names they were read as 0 without a warning pair-assoc reads NA as missing and drops that sample from the trait's tests (--missing-str); missing genotypes are dropped per variant (complete case) NA was read as 0; missing genotypes were mean-imputed Samples are keyed by IID in every loader, and duplicate IIDs are an error a .psam with real family IDs (FID ≠ IID) could misalign genotypes and phenotypes silently Input tables are tab-delimited by default (--space-delim for single-space files) fields were split on any run of whitespace, so IDs with spaces were cut Rank of the covariates computed on scaled columns; constant, duplicate and near-duplicate covariates leave BETA unchanged (with a warning) near-duplicate covariates could shift BETA substantially without a warning pair-assoc no longer requires lexicographic sample order, and stops when no samples overlap it aborted, or ran on with zero samples pair-assoc header starts with TRAIT (was #TRAIT) anqchor accepts both match-prs-pheno warns when fewer than 10 traits have a non-zero weight no warning qpgentools --version none Categorical covariates with --cat-cov-names (REGENIE --catCovarList) in match-prs-pheno, pair-assoc, rect-assoc and region-assoc (commits cb97eb0, 5b811e2) text covariates such as XX/XY had to be recoded to numbers first

anqchor always writes tab-separated, regenie-layout matrices for qpgen (numeric except for categorical covariates, which qpgen encodes) and keys samples by IID, so it does not depend on the delimiter and FID changes. The covariate adjustment, degrees of freedom and missing-value changes do change the numbers: use 0.2.0.

docs.title: Build and discovery
docs.text:
git submodule update --init --recursive
anqchor qpgen build -j 8      # htslib -> qgenlib -> qpgen; produces extern/qpgen/bin/qpgentools
anqchor qpgen check           # path, sha256, git commit, required subcommands

Discovery order: --qpgen / qpgen.binary → $ANQCHOR_QPGEN → qpgentools on PATH → extern/qpgen/bin/qpgentools. An explicit path or $ANQCHOR_QPGEN that does not name an executable is an error (exit code 4).

docs.title: Commands and flags used
docs.text: All genotype input is the prepared 4-column list with absolute prefixes, --pgen-list prepare/genotypes/pgen_list.tsv. All phenotype and covariate input is in regenie layout, so --pheno-format and --cov-format are never needed.

docs.title: Categorical covariates
docs.text:
Covariate files keep categorical covariates as text (sex is XX/XY). Every qpgen command that takes --cov also gets --cat-cov-names with the categorical covariates in that file: the names given with anqchor's --cat-cov-names (config datasets.<ds>.cov_categorical) plus every column with a non-numeric value, detected when the Makefile is built. A command whose covariates include no categorical one gets no --cat-cov-names (--cov-include PC1-5,PEER1-10). qpgen follows REGENIE: a covariate with L levels becomes L − 1 indicator columns, the first level in sorted order is the reference, and --max-cat-levels (default 10) caps the levels. anqchor checks the level counts itself (see covariates), so when a categorical covariate a command uses has N > 10 levels it adds --max-cat-levels N; with 10 or fewer levels the flag is omitted. The log shows the expansion:

NOTICE [...] - Categorical covariate sex: 2 levels (XX, XY); reference XX; 1 indicator columns
NOTICE [...] - Covariate matrix has 6 columns after expanding categorical covariates

The results equal those of the earlier anqchor-side numeric recoding (sex → ½): the covariates span the same column space.

Command Step Flags anqchor passes pair-prs prs.<ref> --pgen-list, --pairs prepare/references/<ref>/pairs.tsv.gz, --out prs/<ref>/prs, --sample (with prs_samples) match-prs-pheno match.<ds>.qpgen --prs, --pheno, --out, --cov and --cat-cov-names (with use_cov), --sample-tsv (with a sample_map), --trait-tsv (when trait IDs differ), --missing-str (non-default), --rint, --mahalanobis + --auto-lambda [--auto-lambda-min-self/-min-best] or --lambda, --min-weight (non-zero), --z-threshold, --z-diff, --threads pair-assoc cis.<ds>.<s>.assoc --pgen-list, --pheno, --pairs prepare/datasets/<ds>/ref.<ref>/pairs.tsv.gz, --out <file>.tsv.gz, --cov and --cat-cov-names (with covariates), --skip-rint (unless --rint) rect-assoc cis.<ds>.<s>.rect.<t> --pgen-list, --pheno, --var-list, --pheno-list, --cov, --cat-cov-names, --rint-after-adj (with --rint), --out rect-assoc trans.<ds>.<s>.rect.<t> as above plus --min-maf, --min-mac, --max-chunk-vars; --pheno-list unless traits: all and trait_chroms: all

For example, the association step of anqchor cis run ... --cov-include sex,PC1-5:

qpgentools pair-assoc --pgen-list prepare/genotypes/pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno prepare/datasets/dataset/pheno.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs prepare/datasets/dataset/ref.reference/pairs.tsv.gz \
  --out cis/dataset/strategies/default/pair_assoc.tsv.gz \
  --cov cis/dataset/strategies/default/cov.regenie.tsv.gz --cat-cov-names sex

and the identity step of anqchor match all with --cov (the --out prefix is a temporary directory inside match/dataset/):

qpgentools match-prs-pheno --prs prs/reference/prs.prs.tsv.gz \
  --pheno prepare/datasets/dataset/pheno.regenie.tsv.gz --out match/dataset/.qpgen.../qpgen \
  --cov prepare/datasets/dataset/cov.regenie.tsv.gz --cat-cov-names sex \
  --rint --z-threshold 1.96 --z-diff 2 --threads 1

Every step's exact command is in steps/<step>.json (commands) and its output in logs/<step>.log. match-prs-pheno runs into a temporary prefix and its outputs are moved into place, so a failed run leaves no partial files.

docs.title: The statistical model of the association tools
docs.text:
For each (variant, trait) with k covariates C (plus an intercept):

  1. the phenotype y is residualised on C: ỹ = (I − P_C) y;
  2. the genotype g is residualised on C: g̃ = (I − P_C) g;
  3. β̂ = g̃ᵀỹ / g̃ᵀg̃, with the residual variance on df = N − 2 − k degrees of freedom, where k is the numerical rank of the covariates (columns of [1, C] minus 1); without covariates df = N − 2;
  4. rint (*_RINT columns of pair-assoc, --rint-after-adj in rect-assoc) replaces ỹ by the rank-based inverse normal transform of ỹ and tests it the same way.
\[ \hat\beta = \frac{\tilde g^\top \tilde y}{\tilde g^\top \tilde g},\qquad \widehat{\mathrm{SE}}^2 = \frac{\tilde y^\top \tilde y - \hat\beta^2\,\tilde g^\top \tilde g}{(N-2-k)\;\tilde g^\top \tilde g} \]

Steps 1-3 are the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell form of the full regression y ~ 1 + C + g, so BETA, SE, TSTAT and LOG10P equal an ordinary least-squares fit with the covariates in the model. pair-assoc and rect-assoc therefore agree on shared pairs: on the example data a cis run with sex, 5 PCs and 10 PEER factors replicates the same 231 (as given) or 230 (with --rint) of 367 pairs at p < 10⁻⁵ with either engine.

Missing genotypes are handled differently: pair-assoc drops the sample from that variant's test (complete case, N = called genotypes = regression sample size); rect-assoc mean-imputes them (N counts called genotypes, df uses all samples). With few missing calls the difference is negligible.

docs.title: Defences kept for older builds
docs.text:
anqchor.qpgen.outputs keeps two fallbacks so that older binaries still run:

  • pair-assoc rows one field short of the header (raw LOG10P missing, before qpgen commit 89eab88): raw LOG10P is recomputed from TSTAT, and the run's cis/<ds>/summary.json lists it under recomputed_log10p;
  • rect-assoc N is always recomputed from N_RR + N_RA + N_AA.

The readers check the columns they rely on and fail with a descriptive error when qpgen's layout changes. These fallbacks do not make an older build's statistics correct; use 0.2.0.

docs.title: Known qpgen behaviours
docs.text:
• Variants are looked up by exact CHROM:POS:REF:ALT, with no allele flips or normalisation; a variant not in the pvar is skipped. anqchor checks presence itself and reports variant_absent.
  • pair-assoc and rect-assoc match samples by identical ID (no map).
  • rect-assoc stops on a missing phenotype or covariate value (including a missing level of a categorical covariate); pair-assoc drops the sample. anqchor's prepared covariate files have no missing values (cov_missing).
  • match-prs-pheno holds an n_prs × n_pheno score matrix in memory (729 × 729 in the example is trivial; 150,000 × 20,000 is about 24 GB). prs_samples limits the PRS samples.
  • The rect-assoc output has 11 + 4 × n_traits columns per variant; keep rectangles small (trait_chroms, traits: reference).

The remaining open qpgen items (allele matching, dosage pgen files not yet tested with the new pair-assoc path) are listed in extern/qpgen/dev/review-2026-10-anqchor.md.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
anqchor answers three questions about an xQTL study. Each one is a separate analysis with its own command, its own inputs and its own run directory. Run the one you need; there is no reason to run them together.

Analysis Question Command Walk-through Identity matching Does each omics sample come from the individual it is labelled with? anqchor match run Sample identity cis evaluation How many known cis pairs replicate with these inputs and covariates? anqchor cis run, then anqchor cis compare Comparing cis runs trans evaluation Do known pairs replicate, do hotspots appear, is the trans scan calibrated? anqchor trans run, then anqchor trans compare trans evaluation

Every example on these pages uses the compact MAGE chromosome 21/22 data that ships with the repository in examples/mage/data/. The example data page describes each file. Commands are run from the repository root.

flowchart TB
    D[Your genotypes, omics matrix, covariates] --> Q{Which question?}
    Q --> M[match run: right individual?]
    Q --> C[cis run: one run per setup]
    Q --> T[trans run: one run per setup]
    C --> CC[cis compare: setups side by side]
    T --> TC[trans compare: setups side by side]

docs.title: When to use each
docs.text:
Identity matching comes first, before any association analysis. Use it when omics samples arrive from a lab or a sequencing core, when you merge batches, and whenever a sample label may have been mixed up. It needs no association test, only the known xQTL effects. The result tells you which samples to keep, relabel or drop before you run cis or trans analyses.

cis evaluation helps you choose analysis settings. It tests only the known cis pairs of a reference, so one run takes seconds. Run it once for each setup you are considering (no covariates, a few PCs, PEER factors, another normalisation, another genotype release), then compare the runs. The setup that replicates more known pairs has more power for those pairs.

trans evaluation tests every variant of the known pairs against every gene of the known pairs. It reports the known cis and trans pairs that replicate, hotspots (1-Mb regions whose variants have trans signals for many genes) at a range of thresholds, and the inflation (λ_GC, QQ plot) of the cross-chromosome tests. Use it to pick covariates before a genome-wide trans scan.

docs.title: Inputs each analysis needs
docs.text:
Input Flag match cis trans Genotypes (PLINK 2 pgen with indexed pvar) --geno-list or --pfile required required required Omics matrix (samples × traits) --pheno required required required Covariates (samples × covariates) --cov recommended optional recommended Reference xQTL pairs (trait variant beta se [pval]) --pairs required required required (or --variants) Trait loci (BED-like) --trait-annot not used only for --assoc-engine rect required Genotype ID ↔ omics ID map --sample-map when IDs differ not accepted not accepted

cis and trans require the omics sample IDs to equal the genotype IDs. Fix labels found by identity matching (or drop those samples) first. The formats are described in Inputs.

docs.title: The commands on the example data
docs.text:
Identity matchingcis evaluationtrans evaluation 
anqchor match all \
  --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --cov examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --out results/match

match all runs the analysis and writes results/match/report/match.html. match run stops at the summary tables, and match report --out results/match re-renders the HTML from them in about a second.

One run per setup. The runs are independent, so they can run at the same time.

D=examples/mage/data

# no covariates
anqchor cis run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --out results/cis/nocov

# 6 covariates
anqchor cis run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --cov-include sex,PC1-5 \
  --out results/cis/basic

# 16 covariates
anqchor cis run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 \
  --out results/cis/peer10

# all 66 covariates
anqchor cis run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --out results/cis/peer60

# compare the four runs
anqchor cis compare results/cis/nocov results/cis/basic results/cis/peer10 results/cis/peer60 \
  --out results/cis/compare

The comparison writes tables and results/cis/compare/report/cis.html. Each run is labelled with its directory name unless you give --label.

One run per covariate set, as for cis. trans also needs the gene loci (--trait-annot) to tell cis from trans cells.

D=examples/mage/data

# no covariates
anqchor trans run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --trait-annot $D/pheno/mage_genes.chr21_22.bed \
  --out results/trans/nocov

# 6 covariates
anqchor trans run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --trait-annot $D/pheno/mage_genes.chr21_22.bed \
  --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --cov-include sex,PC1-5 \
  --out results/trans/basic

# 16 covariates
anqchor trans run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --trait-annot $D/pheno/mage_genes.chr21_22.bed \
  --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 \
  --out results/trans/peer10

# all 66 covariates
anqchor trans run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --trait-annot $D/pheno/mage_genes.chr21_22.bed \
  --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --out results/trans/peer60

Then put the runs side by side:

anqchor trans compare results/trans/nocov results/trans/basic results/trans/peer10 \
  results/trans/peer60 --out results/trans/compare

This writes the comparison tables and results/trans/compare/report/trans.html; anqchor trans report --out results/trans/compare re-renders the page later. Each run is labelled with its directory name unless you give --label. The trans use case adds a fifth run with --rint.

docs.title: Runtime on the example
docs.text:
Measured on a laptop (Apple M2 Max) with qpgen 0.2.0. The data is 729 samples × 367 genes × 256,645 variants on chromosomes 21 and 22.

Command Wall time What runs match all 8 s PRS for 729 genotypes, matching, summaries, report match report 1 s report only cis run (one setup) 6 s 367 known pairs four cis run at once 6 s four independent runs cis compare (four runs) 1 s tables and report trans run (one setup) 8 s 346 variants × 367 genes four trans run at once 9 s four independent runs trans compare (four runs) 1 s tables and report trans report 1 s report only

Re-running a finished command with the same settings does nothing and returns at once. Changing a setting re-runs only the steps it affects.

docs.title: What the example shows
docs.text:
• Identity matching: 727 of 729 samples are confirmed (14 only leniently). Two are unclear. One of them, NA11919, does not match its own genotypes (rank 253 of 729); its best candidate, HG00237, leads the next by only 0.32, so no source is named. Exclude such a sample and check the lab records.
  • cis evaluation: the known pairs come from GTEx, independent of these samples. With no covariates, 178 of the 367 known pairs replicate at p < 10⁻⁵; with sex and 5 PCs, 162; adding 10 PEER factors, 231; with all 66 covariates, 251.
  • trans evaluation: without covariates the cross-chromosome λ_GC is 1.74 and 37 hotspots appear (1-Mb bins with trans signals for ≥ 5 genes at p < 1e-5). Every covariate setup brings λ_GC to between 1.00 and 1.02 (1.02 with sex and 5 PCs, 1.00 with 10 or 60 PEER factors added) with no hotspot and no trans signal at Bonferroni. The reference is cis only, so cis replication matches the cis evaluation and the report shows no trans pairs.

The example reference is independent

The known pairs are GTEx eGenes of EBV-transformed lymphocytes, discovered in GTEx donors, not in the MAGE samples. No setup is favoured by the way the pairs were chosen, so the comparisons measure power. Use an independent reference with your own data too: pairs discovered in the same samples with the same covariates favour that setup.

docs.title: Reproducing a run
docs.text:
Every run directory holds anqchor.resolved.yaml, the complete settings of the run, including those given as flags. To repeat a run exactly:

anqchor cis run --config results/cis/peer10/anqchor.resolved.yaml --out results/cis/peer10_again

run.json in the same directory records each command line that ran in it, the anqchor version, the qpgen binary with its git commit and checksum, and the time each step took.

docs.title: cis evaluation: comparing analysis setups
docs.text:
Question: which analysis setup (covariates, phenotype normalization, genotypes) gives the most power to detect known cis-eQTLs in my data?

Before a genome-wide cis-eQTL scan you have to choose how to model the expression: with no covariates, with sex and genotype PCs, or with some number of hidden factors (PEER factors, PCs of the expression matrix). The choice can change the number of eQTLs you find by a factor of two. anqchor answers the question cheaply. Each anqchor cis run re-tests a list of known cis-eQTL pairs (gene, variant) for one setup and counts how many come back significant. anqchor cis compare then puts several runs side by side.

This page runs the whole comparison on the MAGE example data that ships with the repository: 729 lymphoblastoid cell lines, four covariate setups with the expression as given, and the all-covariate setup once more with a rank-based inverse normal transform (RINT, --rint). The known pairs come from an independent study, GTEx, in the same cell type. The five runs take about 7 seconds together.

Prerequisites

anqchor is installed and qpgen 0.2.0 or later is built (Installation). All commands below are run from the repository root. Results go to results/, which git ignores.

flowchart TB
  A["cis run: nocov"] --> C["cis compare"]
  B["cis run: basic"] --> C
  D["cis run: peer10"] --> C
  E["cis run: peer60"] --> C
  F["cis run: peer60_rint"] --> C
  C --> T["tables + report/cis.html"]

docs.title: Why replication of known pairs measures power
docs.text:
A reference eQTL pair is a (gene, variant) association that another study, or an earlier analysis, found with confidence. If the variant really affects the gene's expression, a better analysis of your data gives a smaller p-value for that pair. Counting how many known pairs reach a given significance level therefore ranks setups by power, using hundreds of true positives at once:

  • it is cheap: only the reference pairs are tested (367 regressions per run here), not every variant against every gene;
  • it is direct: the count is the quantity you care about (how many real eQTLs you can detect), not a proxy such as the variance explained by the covariates;
  • it is comparable: every run tests the same pairs, and the comparison counts pairs tested in every run separately when they differ.

What it does not measure is false positives. A setup that inflates every test statistic (for example by ignoring population structure) also "replicates" more pairs. Check calibration with the rect engine's local controls before you trust a setup that wins without covariates.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
The example data lives in examples/mage/data/ (32 MB), cut down from the MAGE study by examples/mage/make_compact_data.sh: chromosomes 21 and 22, the 729 individuals with expression data, and the genes of the reference eQTLs. The reference eQTLs are from GTEx (example data).

File What it is Flag geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv + geno/mage_chr21.*, geno/mage_chr22.* genotypes, PLINK2: 729 individuals × 256,645 variants with MAF ≥ 5% --geno-list pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz expression, 729 samples × 367 genes --pheno pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz covariates: sex, PC1-5, PEER1-60 (66 columns) --cov reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz 367 known cis-eQTL pairs from GTEx (the reference) --pairs pheno/mage_genes.chr21_22.bed TSS position of each gene --trait-annot (rect engine only)

docs.title: Genotypes
docs.text:
A pgen list tells qpgen which PLINK2 file set covers which chromosome region: CHROM BEG END PREFIX, no header. Relative prefixes are resolved from the list's directory.

examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv
21  1   1000000000  mage_chr21
22  1   1000000000  mage_chr22

Each prefix has a .pgen (genotypes), a .psam (sample IDs) and an indexed variant file .pvar.idx.gz + .pvar.idx.gz.tbi (made with anqchor prepare index-pvar; see Inputs). Variant IDs are CHROM:POS:REF:ALT, which is how the reference names its variants. There are 127,563 variants on chr21 and 129,082 on chr22.

mage_chr21.psam (first lines)
#IID
HG00096
HG00100
mage_chr21.pvar.idx.gz (first lines)
#CHROM  POS      ID               REF  ALT  QUAL  FILTER  INFO  INDEX
21      5031747  21:5031747:G:GA  G    GA   .     .       .     1
21      5031747  21:5031748:GA:G  GA   G    .     .       .     2

docs.title: Expression
docs.text:
regenie layout: one row per sample, FID IID, then one column per gene. Sample IDs are the genotype IDs. The values are already normalized (inverse-normal-transformed TMM).

examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz (first 3 genes)
FID      IID      ENSG00000275993.3:SIK1B  ENSG00000278931.1:bP-2189O9.2  ENSG00000279720.1:SOWAHCP2
HG00096  HG00096  -0.238523                0.224454                       2.54496
HG00100  HG00100  -0.217436                -0.309645                      -0.0685407

docs.title: Covariates
docs.text:
Same layout. sex is text (XX/XY). anqchor treats non-numeric columns as categorical: it keeps the text levels and passes --cat-cov-names sex to qpgen, which encodes them as indicator columns. A run whose --cov-include leaves out sex passes no --cat-cov-names. For categories coded as numbers (a batch number), add --cat-cov-names batch.

examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz (first columns)
FID      IID      sex  PC1         PC2        PC3         PC4        PC5          PEER1       PEER2      ...  PEER60
HG00096  HG00096  XY   -0.0216243  0.0487524  0.00362148  0.0446186  0.00187148   -0.0565679  0.0360434  ...
HG00100  HG00100  XX   -0.0215191  0.0503942  0.00281614  0.040869   0.000118772  0.0722641   0.0525052  ...

PC1-5 are genotype principal components, which capture ancestry; the MAGE samples come from five continental groups of the 1000 Genomes Project. PEER1-60 are hidden factors inferred from the expression matrix. They capture batch, cell-culture and other non-genetic variation shared across many genes.

docs.title: Reference pairs
docs.text:
One row per known eQTL: trait (must match an expression column), variant (CHROM:POS:REF:ALT), beta (effect of the ALT allele), se, and optionally pval.

examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz
trait                          variant         beta       se         pval
ENSG00000275993.3:SIK1B        21:6122794:C:T  -0.448959  0.0888711  8.054e-07
ENSG00000278931.1:bP-2189O9.2  21:9370164:G:A  0.484109   0.10423    5.31901e-06
ENSG00000279720.1:SOWAHCP2     21:9088050:G:A  0.708996   0.180329   0.000107185

These are GTEx v10 eGenes of EBV-transformed lymphocytes (the same cell type as MAGE) on chromosomes 21 and 22 at q ≤ 0.05, each with its sentinel (strongest) variant, kept when the variant is among the genotypes (MAF ≥ 5% in the 729 individuals) and the gene is in the expression data: 367 pairs, 346 distinct variants, 367 genes. beta, se and pval are GTEx's slope, its standard error and nominal p-value. The GTEx donors are not MAGE individuals, so the reference is independent of this data: no setup is favoured by the way the pairs were chosen.

docs.title: Run the five setups
docs.text:
Each anqchor cis run evaluates one setup and writes its tables into its own directory. The first four setups differ only in their covariates; the fifth repeats the all-covariate setup with RINT:

Run Covariates Flags n nocov none no --cov 0 basic sex, PC1, …, PC5 --cov ... --cov-include sex,PC1-5 6 peer10 basic + PEER1, …, PEER10 --cov ... --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 16 peer60 every column of the covariate file --cov ... 66 peer60_rint as peer60, RINT after covariate adjustment --cov ... --rint 66 
anqchor cis run \
    --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
    --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
    --out results/cis/nocov

anqchor cis run \
    --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
    --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
    --cov examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --cov-include sex,PC1-5 \
    --out results/cis/basic

anqchor cis run \
    --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
    --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
    --cov examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 \
    --out results/cis/peer10

anqchor cis run \
    --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
    --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
    --cov examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --out results/cis/peer60

anqchor cis run \
    --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
    --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
    --cov examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --rint \
    --out results/cis/peer60_rint

--cov-include takes covariate names from the header of the covariate file, separated by commas, plus ranges of the form <prefix><first>-<last>: PC1-5 means PC1,PC2,PC3,PC4,PC5. Names are case-sensitive. Without --cov-include every covariate is used; without --cov none is.

A run tests one phenotype transform. By default the phenotypes are tested as given; --rint applies a rank-based inverse normal transform after covariate adjustment. The MAGE expression is already inverse-normal transformed, so peer60_rint is here only to show how a transform is compared: as a run of its own.

The runs are independent, so you can start them at the same time: in five terminals, as five jobs of a cluster scheduler, or in one shell by ending each command with & and then typing wait. Each run prints its steps and a summary line:

[anqchor] running prepare.genotypes
[anqchor] running prepare.reference.reference
[anqchor] running prepare.dataset.dataset
[anqchor] running prepare.mapping.dataset.reference
[anqchor] running cis.dataset.default.inputs
[anqchor] running cis.dataset.default.assoc
[anqchor] running cis.dataset.summarize
ran: prepare.genotypes, prepare.reference.reference, ..., cis.dataset.summarize

Runtime: about 7 seconds of wall time per run on a laptop, and about 7 seconds for all five in parallel. With flags only, the dataset is called dataset, the reference reference and the run's covariate setup default; the run directory name says which setup it is. Running the same command again does nothing (ran: nothing (all steps up to date)).

A run writes tables only, no HTML. To look at one run on its own, render its report: anqchor cis report --out results/cis/peer10 (or use anqchor cis all instead of cis run, which runs and renders in one go).

docs.title: Compare the runs
docs.text:
anqchor cis compare results/cis/nocov results/cis/basic results/cis/peer10 results/cis/peer60 \
    results/cis/peer60_rint --out results/cis/compare

compared 5 run(s): nocov, basic, peer10, peer60, peer60_rint
tables: results/cis/compare
cis report: results/cis/compare/report/cis.html

This takes about 1 second and runs no association test. The first run listed is the baseline that per-gene differences and the relative effective sample size are measured against. Each run is labelled with its directory name; give --label once per run, in order, to choose other labels:

anqchor cis compare results/cis/nocov results/cis/peer60 \
    --label none --label all66 --out results/cis/compare_2

--no-report writes the tables only. To re-render the HTML later (for example after updating anqchor), run

anqchor cis report --out results/cis/compare

which reads the tables of the comparison and rewrites report/cis.html in about 1 second.

docs.title: What comes out
docs.text:
results/cis/compare/
├── report/cis.html            ← start here
├── runs.tsv                   one row per run: what went into it
├── strategies.tsv             one row per run: counts per level, relative N_eff
├── pairs.long.tsv.gz          one row per run × pair
├── traits.tsv                 one row per gene
├── power_curve.tsv            replicated pairs vs −log10 p threshold
├── summary.json               everything above plus the recommendation
├── compare.json               which runs were compared, and the command
└── settings/<label>.anqchor.yaml   exact settings of each run

Column definitions for every file are in Output files and on the cis pipeline page.

docs.title: runs.tsv: what was compared
docs.text:
One row per run with its inputs (paths shortened here):

label        n_geno_samples  n_pheno_samples  cov                             cov_include         n_cov  rint  reference  engine  n_pairs_mapped
nocov        729             729              NA                              NA                  0      0     reference  pair    367
basic        729             729              mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz  sex,PC1-5           6      0     reference  pair    367
peer10       729             729              mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz  sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10  16     0     reference  pair    367
peer60       729             729              mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz  all                 66     0     reference  pair    367
peer60_rint  729             729              mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz  all                 66     1     reference  pair    367

It also has the run directory, the genotype, phenotype and reference paths, and the full list of covariate columns (cov_columns). Check it first: it tells you whether the runs differ in what you meant them to differ in.

docs.title: strategies.tsv: the comparison table
docs.text:
The main result. One row per run (label = run = the run label). n_rep_<level> counts the replicated pairs at each level out of n_tested; frac_rep_<level> is the same as a fraction:

label        rint  n_cov  n_tested  n_rep_sign  n_rep_nominal  n_rep_fdr  n_rep_bonferroni  n_rep_strict  median_log10p  mean_z2  rel_neff  beta_corr  pi1
nocov        0     0      367       339         273            269        196               178           4.77           72.8     1         0.885      0.864
basic        0     6      367       343         266            258        189               162           4.10           60.5     0.829     0.893      0.826
peer10       0     16     367       352         304            300        246               231           8.16           114.2    1.577     0.903      0.913
peer60       0     66     367       353         318            316        269               251           12.15          164.0    2.270     0.903      0.896
peer60_rint  1     66     367       353         319            317        268               251           12.16          151.5    2.097     0.882      0.896

mean_z2 is the mean squared z-score (beta / se) of the tested pairs and rel_neff the effective sample size relative to the first run: (mean z² − 1) / (baseline mean z² − 1) over the pairs tested in every run. With the same 729 samples, peer60 behaves as if it had about 2.3 times as many samples as nocov, because the PEER factors remove expression noise. beta_corr is the correlation of the effect sizes with the reference and pi1 the estimated fraction of tested pairs with a real effect (Storey's π₁ from their p-values).

Other columns: n_variant_absent / n_not_tested (pairs that could not be tested; 0 here), frac_sign_discordant (pairs with the opposite sign: 7.6% for nocov, 3.8% for peer60), bonferroni_log10p (the Bonferroni cut-off, −log10(0.05/367) = 3.87), mean_z2_common, and the common-pair columns:

  • n_common_tested: pairs tested in every compared run (367 here);
  • n_rep_<level>_common: replicated pairs counted over those common pairs only, with FDR and Bonferroni recomputed on them.

Here every run tested the same 367 pairs, so the _common columns equal the plain ones. They matter when runs differ in their reference or genotypes; see Comparing runs with other differences.

docs.title: pairs.long.tsv.gz: every test
docs.text:
One row per (run, pair) with the reference statistics, the study statistics and a 0/1 flag per level. The gene BID under the five runs (some columns omitted):

run          trait                   variant          beta_ref   z_ref  status  beta       se         z       log10p  rep_bonferroni  rep_strict
nocov        ENSG00000015475.19:BID  22:17809432:A:G  -0.245574  -6.37  tested  -0.310253  0.0451848  -6.87   10.85   1               1
basic        ENSG00000015475.19:BID  22:17809432:A:G  -0.245574  -6.37  tested  -0.263623  0.0549377  -4.80   5.71    1               1
peer10       ENSG00000015475.19:BID  22:17809432:A:G  -0.245574  -6.37  tested  -0.240113  0.0439782  -5.46   7.18    1               1
peer60       ENSG00000015475.19:BID  22:17809432:A:G  -0.245574  -6.37  tested  -0.260488  0.0258902  -10.06  21.53   1               1
peer60_rint  ENSG00000015475.19:BID  22:17809432:A:G  -0.245574  -6.37  tested  -0.596281  0.0586096  -10.17  21.96   1               1

The effect estimate is about the same in the four runs on the expression as given, and close to GTEx's (−0.25). What changes is the standard error: the PEER factors remove expression noise, so se drops from 0.045 to 0.026 and −log10 p rises from 10.8 to 21.5. RINT puts the effect on another scale (−0.60), so compare runs that differ in the transform by z or −log10 p, not by beta. z = beta / se and z_ref = beta_ref / se_ref; both refer to the ALT allele. status is tested, variant_absent (variant not in the genotypes) or not_tested. pval_ref and log10p_ref (not shown) come from the reference's pval column.

docs.title: traits.tsv: per gene
docs.text:
One row per gene: best_log10p:<run>, the strongest level it reaches (level:<run>, one of none sign nominal fdr bonferroni strict), delta_log10p:<run> relative to the baseline run (nocov) and best_run (the run with the smallest p-value).

trait                        best_log10p:nocov  level:nocov  ...  best_log10p:peer60  level:peer60  delta_log10p:peer60  best_run
ENSG00000008735.14:MAPK8IP2  3.62               fdr          ...  6.54                strict        2.92                 peer10
ENSG00000015475.19:BID       10.85              strict       ...  21.53               strict        10.68                peer60_rint
ENSG00000025708.14:TYMP      14.49              strict       ...  53.03               strict        38.53                peer60_rint

Use it to find genes that behave differently from the rest. For example, 7 genes reach strict without covariates but not with all 66, and 23 reach it without covariates but not with sex and PCs.

docs.title: power_curve.tsv
docs.text: One row per run and threshold t = 0, 0.5, 1, …: n_replicated pairs are sign-concordant with p < 10^−t, frac_replicated is the fraction of tested pairs. See the table below.

docs.title: summary.json: the recommendation
docs.text:
Everything in machine-readable form: level definitions, level_order, per_run (the strategies.tsv numbers by label), a ranking per level, runs, comparability, warnings, and the recommendation:

"recommended": {
  "key_level": "strict",
  "label": "peer60",
  "reason": "peer60 replicates the most reference pairs at the strict (p < 1e-05) level: 251 of 367 tested, tied with peer60_rint; it replicates more at bonferroni (269 vs 268).",
  "run": "peer60"
}

The recommendation is the run with the most pairs at the strongest level, ties broken by the next weaker levels and then by the order of the runs. comparability records whether all runs used the same reference pairs (same_reference) and which applied RINT (rint).

docs.title: settings/: the exact settings of each run
docs.text: settings/<label>.anqchor.yaml is a copy of each run's anqchor.resolved.yaml: every setting, including the flags, with defaults filled in and paths absolute. It lets you see, and repeat, exactly what each compared run did; see Reproduce a run.

docs.title: Reading the report
docs.text:
Open results/cis/compare/report/cis.html in a browser. It works offline. The title says how many runs are compared; the line below it gives the tested pairs, the samples and the reference file. The first run (nocov) is the baseline. From top to bottom:

  • Replicated pairs by p-value threshold (the power curve): reference pairs replicated (same sign and p below the threshold) against the −log10 p threshold, one line per run. The x axis is log(1 + t) with ticks in −log10 p, so the weak and the strong end are both visible; dashed lines mark p < 0.05 and p < 1e-5. A curve that stays higher further to the right is the more powerful setup. Here peer60 > peer10 > nocov > basic over the whole range, and peer60 and peer60_rint almost overlap. Count / % switches the y axis.
  • Signal strength: first the effective sample size relative to the baseline, a dot per run on a log axis around ×1 with a 95% bootstrap interval: 0.83 (basic), 1.58 (peer10), 2.27 (peer60) and 2.10 (peer60_rint); see rel_neff above. Then the distribution of |z| (or −log10 p) over the pairs tested in every run, one box per run and the reference study as a hollow box.
  • Significant hits: one row per run, with the pairs of the same sign, at p < 0.05 and at p < 1e-5 (count, percentage of tested pairs and a bar). Rows scale to many runs.
  • Agreement with the reference: for the run chosen in the selector (a drop-down list beyond five runs), scatter plots of the effect size, the z-score and −log10 p against the reference study, and of z against the baseline run (points above the diagonal y = x: stronger than the baseline). Each axis has its own scale; effect size and z show a dashed least-squares line through 0 and its slope (for z about √(N_run / N_reference) when the samples differ). Open diamonds mark pairs with the opposite sign to the reference (against the baseline: pairs where the two runs disagree in sign); the correlation is given above each plot. For peer60 the effect sizes correlate with GTEx's at r = 0.90, with a slope of 0.73: the MAGE effects are smaller than the GTEx estimates, as expected when the reference keeps only each gene's strongest variant from a smaller study (the winner's curse). The 14 open diamonds are mostly pairs that are weak in both studies.
  • All pairs: one row per pair with −log10 p in the reference and in every run, and the number of runs where the effect has the opposite sign; such values are red with a minus sign. Sortable, searchable, downloadable; the header and the pair column stay in view.
  • Run details (collapsed): one row per run with its covariates, RINT, samples, the FDR and Bonferroni counts and a link to its saved settings; the FDR and Bonferroni rules; and a link to strategies.tsv with every per-run number.

docs.title: The replication levels
docs.text:
A pair is replicated at a level when its effect has the same sign as in the reference and its p-value passes the level's cut-off. From weakest to strongest on this data:

Level Rule Cut-off here (−log10 p) What it tells you sign same direction as the reference none whether the data and the reference agree at all; random would give 50%. Well below 90%, suspect sample mix-ups, wrong allele coding or a different tissue nominal sign and p < 0.05 1.30 any evidence of the effect; useful for small studies or references from another tissue or population fdr sign and Benjamini-Hochberg q ≤ 0.05 over the run's tested pairs data-dependent: about 1.4–1.5 here discoveries at 5% FDR among these pairs; the replication rate you would report for the reference bonferroni sign and p < 0.05 / n_tested 3.87 (0.05/367) replication that survives correction for every tested pair strict sign and p < 1e-5 5.00 an association strong enough to be found in a scan; the level used to choose a setup (and by the recommendation)

anqchor orders the levels by their actual cut-off, not by name: with tens of thousands of pairs, Bonferroni would be stricter than strict. summary.json (level_order) records the order used. The thresholds can be changed in a configuration file (pipelines.cis.levels).

docs.title: Replicated pairs per level
docs.text:
Out of 367 tested pairs (percent in brackets):

Run n_cov sign nominal FDR 5% Bonferroni strict (1e-5) nocov 0 339 (92.4) 273 (74.4) 269 (73.3) 196 (53.4) 178 (48.5) basic 6 343 (93.5) 266 (72.5) 258 (70.3) 189 (51.5) 162 (44.1) peer10 16 352 (95.9) 304 (82.8) 300 (81.7) 246 (67.0) 231 (62.9) peer60 66 353 (96.2) 318 (86.6) 316 (86.1) 269 (73.3) 251 (68.4) peer60_rint 66 353 (96.2) 319 (86.9) 317 (86.4) 268 (73.0) 251 (68.4)

How to read it:

  • sign shows that the data and the reference agree. 92–96% of the pairs have the GTEx direction. Most of the others are weak in GTEx (median GTEx p 6e-7 against 8e-11 for all pairs) and show no effect here either; a reference from another study always contains some pairs that do not replicate. One pair stands out: HMGN1 has a strong effect in MAGE (p ≈ 1e-20 with all covariates) in the direction opposite to GTEx. Such a pair is worth a closer look (allele coding, the gene model, or a different causal variant in another population), but one pair does not question the data.
  • nominal and FDR rank setups only roughly. FDR follows nominal because most tested pairs are real (π₁ ≈ 0.9), so the Benjamini-Hochberg cut-off is barely stricter than p < 0.05.
  • Bonferroni and strict discriminate. The gaps between setups grow as the threshold gets stricter: nocov and peer60 differ by 4 points at sign, 12 at nominal and 20 at strict. These are the numbers to compare.

docs.title: Along the power curve
docs.text:
From power_curve.tsv: the fraction of the 367 tested pairs that are sign-concordant with p < 10^−t (count in brackets):

Run t = 2 t = 5 t = 8 t = 10 t = 20 nocov 0.687 (252) 0.485 (178) 0.365 (134) 0.316 (116) 0.174 (64) basic 0.654 (240) 0.441 (162) 0.327 (120) 0.272 (100) 0.150 (55) peer10 0.779 (286) 0.629 (231) 0.504 (185) 0.447 (164) 0.256 (94) peer60 0.826 (303) 0.684 (251) 0.594 (218) 0.548 (201) 0.362 (133) peer60_rint 0.831 (305) 0.684 (251) 0.597 (219) 0.548 (201) 0.354 (130)

t = 5 is the strict level. t = 8 is close to the conventional genome-wide threshold (5e-8), which a scan without a cis window would need. t = 10 and t = 20 show the strong eQTLs. The ranking peer60 > peer10 > nocov > basic is the same at every threshold, so the conclusion does not depend on the cut-off. Curves that cross would mean the choice depends on whether you care about weak or strong eQTLs.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
PEER factors give most of the power on this data. Adding 10 PEER factors to sex and PCs lifts the strict count from 162 to 231 (+69 pairs, +43%). Going from 10 to 60 factors adds another 20. The median −log10 p of the known eQTLs rises from 4.1 to 8.2 to 12.2, and the effective sample size relative to nocov from 0.83 to 1.58 to 2.27. The BID example above shows why: the effect size barely changes, but the residual noise shrinks.

Why an independent reference

The reference pairs come from GTEx donors, not from these 729 samples. No setup is therefore favoured by the way the pairs were chosen, and the counts measure power. A reference discovered in the same samples would favour the setup used for its discovery: its pairs are the strongest signals under that model, and every other model looks worse on them. Two things follow from using another study. Not every reference pair is real in this data (π₁ ≈ 0.9, and 14 pairs have the opposite sign even with all covariates). And the effects are smaller here than in GTEx (slope 0.73 for peer60): the reference keeps each gene's strongest variant from a smaller study, which overestimates its effect (the winner's curse). Neither changes the ranking, which compares runs with each other on the same pairs.

More replications without covariates does not mean better. nocov replicates more pairs than basic (178 vs 162 at strict). Do not read this as "sex and PCs hurt". MAGE contains five continental groups, so without PCs, expression differences between populations inflate the test statistics of every variant whose frequency differs between them. The rect engine's local controls show it directly: across chromosomes, where no real cis effect exists, nocov has λ_GC = 1.74 and 445 cells at p < 1e-5, basic has λ_GC = 1.02 and one. Some of nocov's extra replications are inflation. Adjusting for PCs costs a little power and removes false positives; keep them.

RINT makes little difference here. peer60 and peer60_rint differ by at most one pair at any level, the power curves almost overlap and the relative effective sample sizes are 2.27 and 2.10 (slightly lower with RINT). The expression was already inverse-normal transformed before release, so the residuals are close to normal either way. RINT matters more for skewed phenotypes (proteins, metabolites, raw counts). beta_corr is lower with RINT (0.88 vs 0.90) only because RINT puts the effects on a different scale; the same 14 pairs have the opposite sign in both runs.

Recommendation for this data: the all-covariate run on the expression as given, peer60 (tied with peer60_rint at strict, one pair ahead at Bonferroni). The first 10 PEER factors add 69 strict replications and the next 50 add 20, so the gain levels off; a setup with 20 or 30 factors may come close to peer60 (try it). Where that point lies depends on the sample size.

docs.title: Comparing runs with other differences
docs.text:
