Column definitions: Output files. For example, the bins of peer10 with a trans signal at p < 1e-5 (first columns of hotspots.tsv):

chrom  bin_start  bin_end   n_variants  n_genes_p1e-4  n_genes_p1e-5  ...  top_trait               top_variant      top_log10p
22     21000000   22000000  7           1              1              ...  ENSG00000142192.21:APP  22:21694573:C:T  5.15366
22     49000000   50000000  10          1              1              ...  ENSG00000186654.21:PRR5 22:49657211:G:A  5.06097

docs.title: Reading the report
docs.text:
Open results/trans/compare/report/trans.html. The title is Comparing 5 runs: trans-QTL evaluation with anQChor. Under it, one line gives the rectangle (346 variants × 367 genes, 126,982 variant–gene tests, 53,508 across chromosomes), the samples (729) and the reference file, followed by the nocov warning. Each run keeps one color on the whole page. Then three items:

  1. Replicated reference pairs. Do the known eQTLs come back? One block for cis pairs and one for trans pairs; in each, one row per run with the pairs of the same sign as the reference, those with p < 0.05 and those with p < 1e-5, with percentages of the tested pairs. Here the trans block reads "No trans pairs in the reference".
  2. Hotspots. Does a region seem to affect many genes far away? Two rows of buttons choose the threshold (p < 1e-4 … 1e-10, Bonferroni) and the minimum genes per bin (1 … 20) for all runs at once; one row per run shows its number of hotspots out of the 54 bins. Below, for one run (buttons above the chart, or click a run's row): every bin along chromosomes 21 and 22, its height the genes with a trans signal, hotspots in the run's color and the minimum dotted (hover a bar for its genes); the grid of hotspot counts for every threshold and minimum (click a cell to apply it to all runs); and the top 10 hotspot bins with their genes ("Show all 37 bins" for the rest).
  3. Inflation. Are the p-values honest? For the 53,508 cross-chromosome cells: λ_GC per run as a dot (dotted line at 1), the QQ plot with one line per run over the grey 95% band (it opens zoomed on the band, naming nocov, whose line goes off the scale up to −log10 p ≈ 25; Full shows all of it), and the tests observed at p < 1e-3 and p < 1e-5 against the expected 53.5 and 0.5, with the ratio where at least 5 are expected or 10 observed (nocov: ×29 and ×832).

Run details (collapsed) hold, per run, the covariates, rank normalization, samples, rectangle, Bonferroni threshold and a link to its saved settings, then every reference pair with its −log10 p in each run and links to the tables.

docs.title: Replicated reference pairs (367 cis pairs)
docs.text:
Setup same sign p < 0.05 p < 1e-5 nocov 339 (92%) 273 (74%) 178 (49%) basic 343 (93%) 266 (72%) 162 (44%) peer10 352 (96%) 304 (83%) 231 (63%) peer60 353 (96%) 318 (87%) 251 (68%) peer60_rint 353 (96%) 319 (87%) 251 (68%)

The same numbers as the cis analysis of the same setups (cis use case): each reference pair is one cell of the rectangle. PEER factors remove expression noise and raise replication; RINT changes almost nothing for expression that is already normalized.

docs.title: Inflation (53,508 cross-chromosome cells)
docs.text:
Setup λ_GC p < 1e-3 (expected 53.5) p < 1e-5 (expected 0.5) nocov 1.74 1,528 445 basic 1.02 46 1 peer10 1.00 63 1 peer60 1.00 57 0 peer60_rint 1.00 62 0

Without covariates the test statistics are inflated: 29 times the expected count at p < 1e-3 and 832 times at p < 1e-5, with the QQ curve leaving the band from the start. The MAGE samples come from five continental groups, and expression differs between groups for reasons unrelated to any single variant, so every variant whose frequency differs between groups looks associated with many genes. Sex and five genotype PCs already bring λ_GC to 1.02; with PEER factors the curve stays inside the band.

docs.title: Hotspots
docs.text:
Without covariates, nearly every bin is a "hotspot" at any threshold:

nocov, threshold ≥ 1 gene ≥ 2 ≥ 3 ≥ 5 ≥ 10 ≥ 20 p < 1e-4 51 48 48 45 39 28 p < 1e-5 47 46 41 37 31 15 p < 1e-6 45 38 37 33 20 5 Bonferroni (4.1e-7) 41 37 35 33 15 2 p < 5e-8 37 35 34 27 8 1 p < 1e-8 37 35 32 22 5 0 p < 1e-10 31 27 19 10 0 0

The 54 bins with a tested variant hold 37 hotspots at the default (p < 1e-5, ≥ 5 genes), and the same genes (APOBEC3H, CTA-390C10.10, TTC38, SPATC1L, ...) recur in almost every bin: the signature of a confounder, not of master regulators. A stricter threshold shrinks the counts but does not remove the pattern.

With covariates there is no hotspot at p < 1e-5 or below:

Setup p < 1e-4: bins with ≥ 1 / ≥ 2 / ≥ 3 genes p < 1e-5: ≥ 1 gene Bonferroni basic 12 / 2 / 1 4 0 peer10 17 / 1 / 1 2 0 peer60 9 / 1 / 0 0 0 peer60_rint 7 / 2 / 0 0 0

The few single-gene bins at p < 1e-5 (for example APP on chr21 from the chr22:21-22 Mb bin, p ≈ 7e-6 in basic and peer10) are in line with the 0.5 false positives expected among the 53,508 cross-chromosome cells and about 1.2 among all 120,796 trans cells; none passes Bonferroni.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
• Calibrate first. With λ_GC = 1.74, every trans number of the nocov run is suspect; on the comparison page its dot sits far right of the dotted line and its QQ line leaves the band at once. Basic covariates fix most of the inflation; PEER factors finish the job and also raise cis replication. Choose the setup that keeps λ_GC near 1 and replicates the most cis pairs: here peer60 (or peer10 if you prefer fewer covariates).
  • Hotspots that vanish with covariates were artefacts. When many bins hit the same few genes, suspect a shared confounder (ancestry, batch) before biology.
  • Strong trans hits that survive good covariates are often paralogs or duplicated regions (reads or variant calls mapped to the wrong copy). Check the gene names before calling a trans-eQTL.
  • The threshold must match the number of tests. This rectangle has 120,796 trans cells; a genome-wide scan has billions. Read the grid at Bonferroni, not at a fixed p.
  • A cis-only reference tests only half of item 1. Trans replication needs a reference with trans pairs; its regions are then also left out of the inflation cells.

docs.title: Try it yourself
docs.text:
Another hotspot minimum or bin width. The report already shows every threshold and the minimums 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 and 20 without re-running. Another bin width needs a new run; give it its own directory so that the original run stays as it was:

anqchor trans run "${IN[@]}" "${COV[@]}" --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 --hotspot-bin-bp 500000 --out results/trans/peer10_bin500
anqchor trans compare results/trans/peer10 results/trans/peer10_bin500 --out results/trans/compare_bins

The comparison warns that the bin widths differ (hotspot counts are then not comparable one to one) and shows each run's bins with its own width.

Test every gene. --traits all tests every gene of the expression file; the example file holds exactly the 367 reference genes, so the rectangle is the same here. With a full expression matrix, --traits all is a preview of a genome-wide trans scan restricted to the reference variants.

Another variant set. --variants FILE (one CHROM:POS:REF:ALT per line) replaces the reference's variants, for example with the sentinel variants of a GWAS.

docs.title: Equivalent configuration
docs.text:
examples/mage/trans.yaml is the peer60 run as a configuration file, with a strict level (p < 1e-8, no flag) added to the hotspot grid:

anqchor trans run --config examples/mage/trans.yaml --out results/trans_config

Its run directory compares like any other, for example anqchor trans compare results/trans/peer60 results/trans_config --out results/trans/compare_config.

A configuration file runs one setup, like the flags (pipelines.trans.strategies has one entry; rint: true instead of --rint). anqchor.resolved.yaml in any run directory is a complete configuration file for that run: anqchor trans run --config results/trans/peer10/anqchor.resolved.yaml --out results/trans/peer10_again reproduces it.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Message Cause and fix trait_chroms 'genotyped' keeps none of the … traits the genes have no locus, or none is on a genotyped chromosome: give --trait-annot, or set trait_chroms: all 'transforms' (...) is no longer accepted a configuration written for an older anqchor; remove transforms and set rint: true for RINT (one transform per run) a trans run evaluates one set of inputs, got N a configuration with several strategies: make one run per covariate set pipelines.trans.levels.fdr is no longer used remove fdr from pipelines.trans.levels the trans summaries … are from an older anqchor trans report on a run made before this version: run anqchor trans run again on the directory … is not an anqchor run directory / … is not a trans run directory trans compare was given a directory that is not a finished trans run: check the paths, or run it first … missing trans/…; re-run 'anqchor trans run --out …' a run directory lost a summary table: run the same trans run again … given more than once the same run directory appears twice in trans compare duplicate run label(s) … two runs got the same label (two directories with the same name and the same parent directory name): give one --label per run --out … is a run directory / --out … holds a cis comparison trans compare --out must be a new directory or an earlier trans comparison the runs tested different variant–gene tests (…) (warning) the runs differ in variants, genes or tests: λGC, observed counts and hotspots are then each over the run's own tests … is a cis comparison; use 'anqchor cis report …' trans report on a cis compare directory p-values inflated (λGC … across chromosomes, above 1.1) (warning) the setup is miscalibrated: add covariates (ancestry PCs, expression factors)

docs.title: Data provenance
docs.text:
The compact example data in examples/mage/data/ was produced by examples/mage/make_compact_data.sh from the MAGE lymphoblastoid RNA-seq data (729 samples), the 1000 Genomes (NYGC) high-coverage genotypes of chromosomes 21 and 22, and the GTEx v10 EBV-transformed lymphocyte eGenes; see Example data.

More on the analysis itself: trans: replication, hotspots and inflation.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: The terms below are used consistently in the commands, configuration, file names, logs and reports.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Genotype set One PLINK2 dataset, possibly split by chromosome, described by a qpgen pgen list (CHROM BEG END PREFIX) or a single prefix (pfile). Each prefix needs .pgen, .psam and an indexed pvar .pvar.idx.gz + .tbi. All files of a set must share one sample list. See Inputs. Reference A set of known xQTL effects: a pair file with trait variant beta se [pval] per row. Variants are CHROM:POS:REF:ALT (CPRA), with ALT the effect allele. Kind cis (pairs required) or trans (pairs and/or a variant list). A reference feeds the PRS of match, the replication test of cis, and the variants and known positives of trans. For evaluating analysis choices, use a reference discovered in other samples (for example GTEx): pairs discovered in your own samples, with your own covariates, replicate best under those same choices by construction. Dataset One omics phenotype matrix (traits × samples) with optional covariates, trait annotation and sample map. A flags-only run has one dataset called dataset; a configuration file may define several (rnaseq, proteomics, ...). The omics label is free text shown in reports. Trait One molecular phenotype (gene, protein, metabolite, CpG), identified by a string ID. Sample map A table geno_id pheno_id linking genotype IDs to omics sample IDs, used only by match. Absent means identical IDs. Trait map / trait-ID rule

How a reference's trait IDs are matched to a dataset's trait IDs. A rule is applied to both sides and IDs match when the transformed keys agree:

trait_id_rule Transformation ENSG00000227232.5:WASH7P becomes ENSG00000227232.5 becomes as_is (default) none unchanged unchanged before_colon part before the first : ENSG00000227232.5 unchanged strip_version drop a trailing .<digits> unchanged (no trailing version) ENSG00000227232 before_colon_strip_version both ENSG00000227232 ENSG00000227232

For anything else, give an explicit trait map file (ref_trait pheno_trait, two columns). When no trait maps, the error names the rule that would have worked best. Trait annotations (trait_annot) are matched to phenotype IDs with the same rules, automatically: the rule matching the most traits wins.

docs.title: Analyses
docs.text:
Analysis One of the three questions anqchor answers, each run on its own with its own command: identity matching (anqchor match), cis evaluation (anqchor cis) and trans evaluation (anqchor trans). Internally each analysis is a pipeline of steps; the words are used interchangeably in file and step names (match/, report.cis). PRS Polygenic score of each genotyped sample for each reference trait, computed by qpgentools pair-prs. It depends only on the genotypes and the reference (prs/<ref>/). Transform

How the phenotype is tested after covariate adjustment:

  • as given (raw): the phenotype is residualised on the covariates (with intercept) and regressed on the genotype, which is residualised on the same covariates.
  • rint: the covariate-adjusted phenotype is rank-based inverse-normal transformed (Blom offsets, average ranks for ties) and then tested the same way.

A cis or trans run tests one transform: the phenotypes as given, or RINT with --rint; raw and RINT are compared as two runs (with cis compare or trans compare).

docs.title: Runs and comparisons
docs.text: Run One execution of an analysis on one set of inputs: genotypes, phenotypes, covariates (optionally a subset of their columns, --cov-include), for cis and trans the phenotype transform (--rint), and a reference. A run writes into its own run directory (--out). To evaluate an alternative, such as other covariates, another normalisation or another genotype set, start another run into another directory. Runs are independent and can run in parallel. Comparison anqchor cis compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR reads finished cis runs and puts them side by side in one set of tables and one report. The runs may differ in any input. Each run is identified by a label (its directory name unless --label is given). A comparison counts replication over each run's own tested pairs and, separately, over the pairs tested in every run (the _common columns), so runs with different genotypes or references stay comparable. Run directory The output directory of a run (--out). It holds the complete settings (anqchor.resolved.yaml), the provenance (run.json), the generated Makefile, step logs, every output and, once rendered, the report. See Running. Run, report, all Each analysis separates computing from rendering. run computes the summary tables; report renders the HTML from those tables in about a second and runs no analysis; all does both. Strategy A term of the configuration file, not of the command line. In a config file, a strategies list under pipelines.cis or pipelines.trans defines several named covariate/phenotype choices evaluated inside one run. Prefer one run per choice: a flags-only cis run or trans run has a single strategy called default. A cis run's and trans results are labelled with the run directory name (a trans configuration has exactly one strategy). cis runs are compared with cis compare, trans runs with trans compare.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text: Step One unit of work with declared input files, output files and commands, named with dots (prepare.dataset.rnaseq, cis.rnaseq.default.assoc). A step is either a qpgen command or a Python step run as python -m anqchor _step <name> --run-dir .. Steps form a graph and run through a generated Makefile, so a repeated command re-runs only what changed.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Match status and group

qpgen's per-sample status is kept verbatim; anqchor adds a coarse group.

Group qpgen statuses Meaning PASS SELF_BEST the labelled genotype is the best match WARN SELF_LENIENT, UNCLEAR the labelled genotype is not first, but its Z is above z_threshold (SELF_LENIENT), or nothing is clear (UNCLEAR) FAIL SINGLE_NEW_BEST, MULTI_NEW_BEST (of a mapped sample) one (or a block of) other genotype(s) matches clearly better NO_TEST NO_SELF, NO_OBS_TRAITS, and every unmapped sample there is no label to confirm

An unmapped sample with SINGLE_NEW_BEST is a rescue candidate. Rules: match pipeline.

Replication level

How strongly a known pair is reproduced. Every level requires sign concordance (sign(beta_ref) == sign(beta)). With the cis defaults and the 367 pairs of the example data, from weakest to strongest (the order is computed from each level's actual p cut-off, so it can change with the number of tested pairs):

Level Rule (cis defaults) sign sign concordance alone (always reported) nominal sign and p < 0.05 fdr sign and Benjamini-Hochberg q ≤ 0.05 over the tested pairs of the run bonferroni sign and p < 0.05 / n_tested strict sign and p < 1e-5

The cutoffs are configurable under levels; a level set to null (or bonferroni: false) is not reported. trans replicates its reference pairs at the same sign, p < 0.05 and p < 1e-5; its own levels (nominal: 1e-5, optional strict, Bonferroni over the trans cells) are thresholds of the hotspot grid.

Pair status Every mapped reference pair is tested, variant_absent (its variant is not in the genotype pvar under that exact CPRA) or not_tested (variant present, but qpgen wrote no result or no finite statistic). Unresolved = absent + not tested; cis fails when more than max_unresolved_fraction (20%) of the pairs are unresolved. cis and trans (trans) A (variant, gene) cell of the trans rectangle, or a reference pair, is cis when the variant is on the gene's chromosome within cis_window_bp (1 Mb) of the gene start, and trans otherwise: on another chromosome (cross-chromosome) or farther on the same one. Genes without a locus are counted apart. Inflation (λ_GC, QQ) uses the cross-chromosome cells, leaving out the regions of the reference's trans pairs. Hotspot (trans) A bin of hotspot_bin_bp (1 Mb) whose variants have trans signals (p below a threshold) for at least k distinct genes, genes in cis with the bin not counted. The report shows the counts for a grid of thresholds and k. λ_GC Genomic control inflation: median χ²(1) of the cells divided by 0.4549. Values near 1 mean a calibrated null; anqchor warns above 1.1 or below 1/1.1.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Every analysis can be run from command-line flags alone, and that is the usual way to start. A YAML configuration file is the alternative when you want the settings in a file, need options that have no flag (for example missing_str, trait_chroms or the replication levels), or want to repeat a run exactly.

Every run writes its complete settings, flags included, to <run>/anqchor.resolved.yaml (defaults filled in, paths absolute). That file is a valid configuration file. After the flags-only run

D=examples/mage/data
anqchor cis run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 \
  --out results/cis/peer10

the command

anqchor cis run --config results/cis/peer10/anqchor.resolved.yaml --out results/cis/peer10_again

reproduces it exactly (see Running).

The file is validated by pydantic models (src/anqchor/config/model.py). Unknown keys are errors, so typos fail at load time with a message naming the dotted location (exit code 2):

error: invalid configuration:
  pipelines.cis.levels.strcit: Extra inputs are not permitted

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
The flags of the example data,

D=examples/mage/data
anqchor cis run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --out results/cis/peer60

can be kept in a file instead. Saved as results/mage.yaml (relative paths are resolved against the file's directory):

genotypes:
  pgen_list: ../examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv
references:
  reference:
    pairs: ../examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz
datasets:
  dataset:
    pheno: ../examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz
    cov: ../examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz

anqchor cis run   --config results/mage.yaml --out results/cis/peer60_config
anqchor match run --config results/mage.yaml --out results/match_config

anqchor <analysis> run --config FILE runs that one analysis with the file's genotypes, reference and dataset; each analysis is still a separate command with its own run directory. With the names dataset and reference used by the flags, the outputs have the same paths as a flags-only run. The enabled keys under pipelines only matter for the top-level anqchor run (see Command line).

docs.title: Flags and configuration keys
docs.text:
Flag Configuration key --geno-list FILE / --pfile PREFIX genotypes.pgen_list / genotypes.pfile --pairs FILE references.<name>.pairs (<name> = --reference-name, default reference) --pheno FILE, --pheno-format datasets.<name>.pheno, .pheno_format (<name> = --dataset-name, default dataset) --cov FILE, --cov-format datasets.<name>.cov, .cov_format --cat-cov-names NAMES datasets.<name>.cov_categorical (comma-separated → list) --trait-annot FILE datasets.<name>.trait_annot --trait-id-rule RULE datasets.<name>.trait_id_rule --sample-map FILE datasets.<name>.sample_map --cov-include NAMES (cis, trans) pipelines.<analysis>.strategies: [{name: default, cov: {include: [NAMES]}}] --assoc-engine (cis) pipelines.cis.assoc_engine --rint / --no-rint (cis, trans) pipelines.<analysis>.rint --out DIR out_dir --threads N, --qpgen PATH qpgen.threads, qpgen.binary --plotlyjs report.plotlyjs

The match and trans flags map to the keys of the same name under pipelines.match and pipelines.trans (--z-threshold → z_threshold, --mahalanobis → mahalanobis: true, --cis-window-bp → cis_window_bp, --hotspot-min-traits → hotspot_min_traits, ...). The command-line reference lists them.

The reference p-value column

--pairs reads the trait variant beta se columns and, when the file has one, a column named pval, reported as pval_ref. A p-value column with another name needs columns: {pval: NAME} in a configuration file. Replication does not use it.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Paths. Relative paths in the file are resolved against the directory of the config file; paths given as command-line flags are resolved against the current directory. A file: prefix is optional (traits: file:my_traits.txt). ~ is expanded.

Precedence. Command-line flags > YAML file > model defaults. Unset flags never override the file. A genotype flag (--geno-list, --pfile) replaces the file's whole genotypes section. Input flags such as --pheno describe a dataset named by --dataset-name (default dataset); when the file defines exactly one dataset under another name, the flags override that dataset instead of adding a second one (likewise --pairs and the single reference). --cov-include replaces the file's whole strategies list for that analysis.

Names. Reference, dataset and strategy names use letters, digits, _, ., - and start with a letter or digit. They appear in step and file names.

Several references. When more than one reference is defined, every enabled pipeline must name its reference.

docs.title: version, project, out_dir
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning version 1 1 configuration schema version project string anqchor project name shown in reports out_dir path anqchor_out run directory; --out overrides it

docs.title: qpgen
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning binary path or null null explicit qpgentools; null = discovery (--qpgen, $ANQCHOR_QPGEN, PATH, extern/qpgen/bin) threads int ≥ 1 1 threads passed to match-prs-pheno --threads (--threads flag). The other qpgen commands are single-threaded. Not part of any step signature: changing it re-runs nothing.

docs.title: genotypes
docs.text:
Exactly one of:

Key Type Meaning pgen_list path qpgen pgen list, CHROM BEG END PREFIX (or 6 columns) pfile path one PLINK2 prefix with .pgen, .psam, .pvar.idx.gz (+ .tbi)

See Inputs: genotypes.

docs.title: references.<name>
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning kind cis | trans cis a cis reference needs pairs; a trans reference needs pairs or variants pairs path — pair file with a header (trait, variant, beta, se, optional pval) variants path — trans only: one CHROM:POS:REF:ALT per line columns.trait string trait column name of the trait ID columns.variant string variant column name of the CPRA variant ID columns.beta string beta effect of the ALT allele columns.se string se standard error columns.pval string or null null optional p-value column, carried into outputs; null reads a column named pval when present

match and cis need a reference with pairs (effect sizes for the PRS, pairs to replicate).

docs.title: datasets.<name>
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning omics string omics label shown in reports pheno path required phenotype matrix pheno_format regenie | tensorqtl | tsv-sample-row | tsv-sample-col regenie layout trait_annot path null trait loci, BED-like or trait chrom start end; a tensorqtl phenotype provides loci itself cov path null covariate matrix (the dataset's default covariates) cov_format as pheno_format regenie covariate layout cov_categorical list of names [] force these covariates to be categorical, e.g. a batch number (non-numeric ones are detected automatically, see covariates); flag --cat-cov-names a,b. Categorical covariates keep their text levels in the prepared file and are passed to qpgen as --cat-cov-names, which encodes L levels as L − 1 indicators (anqchor adds --max-cat-levels when a covariate has more than qpgen's default of 10). A non-numeric column with more than 20 levels (and more than a tenth of the samples) must be listed here cov_missing error | drop_samples | impute_mean error missing covariate values missing_str list of strings ["NA"] spellings of a missing value in phenotype and covariate files; an empty cell is always missing sample_map path null match only: geno_id pheno_id table; null = identical IDs trait_id_rule as_is | before_colon | strip_version | before_colon_strip_version | file:<path> as_is how reference trait IDs map to dataset trait IDs (rules); file:<path> = trait_map: <path> trait_map path null explicit ref_trait pheno_trait file; overrides the rule

docs.title: pipelines.match
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning enabled bool true include in the top-level anqchor run; anqchor match run ignores it datasets list or null null (all) datasets to check reference name or null null (the only reference) reference for the PRS prs_samples all | path all genotype IDs (one per line) to compute PRS for; all scores every genotyped sample, which improves calibration and enables rescue use_cov bool true adjust phenotypes for the dataset covariates rint bool true rank-based inverse normal transform after adjustment (--rint) mahalanobis bool false whiten correlated traits (--mahalanobis, slower); default scores traits as independent lambda auto | number in [0, 1] auto with mahalanobis: auto → --auto-lambda when at least min_self_for_auto samples are mapped, else --lambda 0.5 (with a warning); a number → --lambda min_self_for_auto int ≥ 1 100 mapped-sample minimum for --auto-lambda z_threshold float 1.96 Z above which a non-best own genotype is a lenient match z_diff float ≥ 0 2.0 Z gap that makes a leading genotype clear min_weight float 0.0 --min-weight (passed only when non-zero)

docs.title: pipelines.cis
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning enabled bool true datasets list or null null (all) reference name or null null reference whose pairs are replicated assoc_engine pair | rect pair pair-assoc over the pairs, or rect-assoc over the reference's variants × traits strategies list of strategies [{name: default}] covariate/phenotype choices of this run; --cov-include sets a single one. First = baseline; names unique rint bool false rank-based inverse normal transform of the phenotypes after covariate adjustment (--rint); false tests the phenotypes as given. A cis run tests one transform; compare raw and RINT as two runs levels.nominal float in (0, 1) or null 0.05 sign and p < value levels.strict float or null 1e-5 sign and p < value levels.bonferroni bool true sign and p < 0.05 / n_tested levels.fdr float or null 0.05 sign and BH q ≤ value max_unresolved_fraction float in [0, 1] 0.2 fail when more of the mapped pairs are variant_absent or not_tested

docs.title: pipelines.trans
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning enabled bool true datasets list or null null (all) reference name or null null variants reference | path reference the reference's present variants, or a CPRA list file traits reference | all | path reference the reference's mapped traits (the initial test rectangle), every dataset trait, or a file of trait IDs (first column) trait_chroms genotyped | all | list genotyped keep traits whose locus is on these chromosomes: genotyped = the genotype set's chromosomes; a list such as [21, 22] (either style); all = no restriction. Traits without a locus are kept only with all known_pairs bool true replicate the reference pairs and leave the regions of its trans pairs out of the inflation cells (needs pairs) strategies list of one strategy [{name: default}] the covariate/phenotype choice of this run (exactly one entry); --cov-include sets it rint bool false rank-based inverse normal transform of the phenotypes after covariate adjustment (--rint, rect-assoc --rint-after-adj); false tests the phenotypes as given. A trans run tests one transform cis_window_bp int ≥ 0 1000000 a variant within this distance of the gene start on the same chromosome is cis; every other pair is trans (--cis-window-bp) min_maf float in [0, 0.5) 0.01 rect-assoc --min-maf min_mac float ≥ 0 1.0 rect-assoc --min-mac levels.nominal float in (0, 1) 1e-5 a trans signal is p < value: the report's default hotspot threshold and the cut-off of pairs.sig.tsv.gz levels.strict float or null null an extra threshold for the hotspot grid (e.g. 1e-8) levels.bonferroni bool true add p < 0.05 / trans cells tested to the hotspot grid hotspot_bin_bp int ≥ 1 1000000 width of the bins that thin trans signals for hotspots (--hotspot-bin-bp) hotspot_min_traits int ≥ 1 5 genes with a trans signal a bin needs to be a hotspot; the report's default (--hotspot-min-traits) max_chunk_vars int ≥ 1 100 rect-assoc --max-chunk-vars max_sig_rows int ≥ 1 1000000 cap on rows in pairs.sig.tsv.gz (strongest kept)

Accepted spellings: variants/traits: reference:<name> name the reference and set reference; known_pairs: reference:<name> means true, known_pairs: null means false. All three must name the same reference.

Keep the rectangle small

traits: all with trait_chroms: all tests every variant against every trait. With a genome-wide expression matrix that is 20,000+ traits and an output of 11 + 4 × n_traits columns per variant. Prefer trait_chroms: genotyped (the default) or traits: reference.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
A strategy is a named covariate/phenotype choice inside one run. On the command line a run has exactly one, called default: all covariates of --cov, the subset named by --cov-include, or none when --cov is omitted. In a configuration file:

  • cis: keep one strategy per run (as examples/mage/cis.yaml does) and compare runs with anqchor cis compare. A list of several strategies still works; their results then share one run directory and are labelled <run label>:<strategy> in a comparison.
  • trans: exactly one strategy per run: start one trans run per covariate set (--cov-include), each into its own directory. A list of several strategies is an error that says so. Compare the runs with anqchor trans compare.

Each entry of pipelines.cis.strategies and pipelines.trans.strategies:

Key Type Default Meaning name string required unique within the pipeline cov default | null | {include: [...]} | {file: path, format: ...} | path default default = all dataset covariates; null = none; include = a named subset (ranges PEER1-15; unknown names are errors); file = a separate covariate file, checked like the dataset's, categorical covariates kept as text (a bare path is shorthand). Each strategy passes qpgen --cat-cov-names with the categorical covariates it uses (recorded as cat_cov_names in strategy.json) pheno path null alternative phenotype matrix (e.g. another normalisation) for this strategy pheno_format layout regenie layout of pheno

One transform per run

Strategies have no transforms key: a cis or trans run tests the phenotypes as given, or with pipelines.<analysis>.rint: true (--rint) their RINT after covariate adjustment. Configuration files written for earlier versions with transforms under pipelines.cis.strategies or pipelines.trans.strategies are rejected with a message saying what to write instead: remove the key ([raw]), set rint: true ([rint]), or make two runs ([raw, rint]). pipelines.trans.levels.fdr is likewise rejected.

The forms of cov, written for a file next to examples/mage/cis.yaml (a run normally has one of these entries):

strategies:
  - {name: peer60, cov: default}                                    # every covariate (= --cov)
  - {name: peer10, cov: {include: [sex, PC1-5, PEER1-10]}}          # = --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10
  - {name: nocov, cov: null}                                        # no covariates
  - {name: filecov, cov: {file: data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz, format: regenie}}

The last entry reads its covariates from a file of its own instead of the dataset's cov (here the same file, so it gives the same results as peer60). A pheno entry works the same way for a phenotype matrix with another normalisation.

docs.title: report
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning plotlyjs embed | cdn embed embed writes plotly.js into each page (works offline; the example reports are 5-10 MB each); cdn loads it from the CDN (small files; offline, each chart area shows a notice suggesting --plotlyjs embed and the tables still work)

docs.title: Annotated examples
docs.text:
examples/mage/cis.yaml, the all-covariate cis run of the example data:

# anqchor cis: replication of known cis-eQTLs for ONE set of inputs.
#
# Each cis run evaluates one set of inputs (genotypes, phenotypes, covariates, phenotype
# transform, reference).
# To compare analysis setups, run 'anqchor cis run' once per setup (into separate
# directories; the runs are independent and can run in parallel) and compare them with
# 'anqchor cis compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR'.
#
# This file is the all-covariate run of the MAGE example (chr21/22 compact data in data/).
# It is equivalent to the flags-only command
#
#   anqchor cis run --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
#       --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
#       --cov examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
#       --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
#       --out results/cis/peer60
#
# except for the dataset and reference names (rnaseq and gtex_lcl here, dataset and
# reference with flags). Paths are relative to this file. From the repository root:
#
#   anqchor cis run --config examples/mage/cis.yaml --out results/cis_config
#
version: 1
project: mage_cis
out_dir: ../../results/cis_config      # overridden by --out

genotypes:
  # qpgen pgen list (CHROM BEG END PREFIX): 729 individuals, 256,645 variants (MAF >= 5%).
  pgen_list: data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv

references:
  gtex_lcl:
    kind: cis
    # 367 GTEx v10 LCL eGenes on chr21/22 with their sentinel variant (columns trait variant
    # beta se pval), from donors independent of MAGE.
    pairs: data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz
    columns: {trait: trait, variant: variant, beta: beta, se: se, pval: pval}

datasets:
  rnaseq:
    omics: rnaseq
    # 729 samples x 367 genes, regenie layout (FID IID gene...), IDs 'ENSG...:GENE'.
    pheno: data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz
    pheno_format: regenie
    # Gene TSS loci (BED, same IDs). Not needed by the default pair engine; the rect engine
    # uses them to split its local controls into same- and cross-chromosome cells.
    trait_annot: data/pheno/mage_genes.chr21_22.bed
    # sex (XX/XY, categorical: passed to qpgen as text), PC1-5, PEER1-60: 66 covariates.
    cov: data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz
    cov_format: regenie
    trait_id_rule: as_is               # reference and expression trait IDs are identical

pipelines:
  match: {enabled: false}              # this file is for the cis analysis only
  trans: {enabled: false}
  cis:
    reference: gtex_lcl
    assoc_engine: pair                 # pair (pair-assoc) | rect (rect-assoc over variants x traits)
    # One strategy = this run's covariates. 'cov: default' uses every column of the
    # dataset's cov file (same as omitting --cov-include). For a subset, write e.g.
    #   cov: {include: [sex, PC1-5, PEER1-10]}      (= --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10)
    # and for no covariates 'cov: null' (= omitting --cov).
    strategies:
      - {name: default, cov: default}
    # Phenotype transform of this run: false = the expression as given; true = rank-based
    # inverse normal transform after covariate adjustment (= --rint). One transform per run.
    rint: false
    levels: {nominal: 0.05, fdr: 0.05, bonferroni: true, strict: 1.0e-5}
    max_unresolved_fraction: 0.2

examples/mage/match.yaml (identity matching) follows the same pattern. Each file's header shows the equivalent flags-only command.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
anqchor needs three kinds of input: a genotype set, a reference of known xQTLs, and an omics dataset (phenotypes, optionally covariates and trait loci). On the command line they are --geno-list (or --pfile), --pairs, and --pheno with --cov, --trait-annot and --sample-map. Everything is validated and normalised by the prepare.* steps before qpgen runs, so most input problems fail early with a clear message (exit code 3, with the step log named).

The example data in examples/mage/data/ has one file of each kind; the example data page shows the first lines of each.

docs.title: Genotypes
docs.text:
PLINK2 files, one prefix per chromosome or one for everything. Each prefix needs:

File Notes PREFIX.pgen genotypes (hard calls or dosages) PREFIX.psam samples; header #IID ... or #FID IID ...; IIDs are the genotype sample IDs PREFIX.pvar.idx.gz + .tbi indexed pvar: a 9-column bgzipped, tabix-indexed VCF-like file (#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO INDEX) with a 1-based INDEX column in pgen row order

The indexed pvar is what qpgen uses to look variants up by CHROM:POS:REF:ALT. Create it with:

anqchor prepare index-pvar --pfile geno/chr21
# wrote geno/chr21.pvar.idx.gz (127563 variants) and geno/chr21.pvar.idx.gz.tbi

It reads PREFIX.pvar, PREFIX.pvar.zst (needs zstd) or PREFIX.pvar.gz; a headerless pvar is read in .bim column order. It needs bgzip and tabix and checks that the number of records written equals the number read back. The pvar must be sorted for tabix.

docs.title: The pgen list
docs.text:
Describe a multi-file genotype set with a qpgen pgen list, one row per file, whitespace separated, no header (# lines ignored):

21  1  2000000000  /data/geno/chr21
22  1  2000000000  /data/geno/chr22

Columns are CHROM BEG END PREFIX. The 6-column form CHROM BEG END PGEN PSAM PIVAR is also accepted; anqchor recognises the PSAM and PIVAR fields by name or content because qpgen's parser and documentation disagree on their order. Write a list with:

anqchor prepare pgen-list --prefix-template '/data/geno/chr{chrom}' --chroms 1-22,X --out geno.list.tsv

CHROM is read from each file's first pvar record so it matches the pvar spelling; every prefix must have .pgen, .psam, .pvar.idx.gz and .tbi (--no-check skips the checks).

For a single prefix use --pfile PREFIX (genotypes.pfile in a configuration file).

What prepare.genotypes does:

  • Resolves relative prefixes against the list's directory and then up to three parent directories (lists are often written relative to a project directory); qpgen itself would resolve them against the current directory.
  • Checks that every file exists, that all psam files list the same samples in the same order, and that sample IDs are unique.
  • Detects the chromosome style from the first pvar record (chr21 → chr, 21 → plain) and requires the list's CHROM column to use the same style.
  • Writes prepare/genotypes/pgen_list.tsv in the 4-column form with absolute prefixes. Files whose names are not PREFIX.{pgen,psam,pvar.idx.gz} are symlinked under prepare/genotypes/links/ so that the 4-column form always works.

Variant IDs

qpgen matches variants by exact CHROM:POS:REF:ALT string equality. anqchor rewrites the chromosome of reference variants to the genotype style (chr22:… ↔ 22:…), but does not flip alleles or left-normalise indels. Variants that do not match are reported as variant_absent with an SNV/indel split.

docs.title: Phenotypes
docs.text:
A traits × samples matrix in one of four layouts (pheno_format):

Format Orientation Header Notes regenie (default) rows = samples FID IID trait1 trait2 … canonical internal format tensorqtl rows = traits #chr start end phenotype_id s1 s2 … first four column names matched case-insensitively with optional # (#Chr is fine; chrom accepted); also provides trait loci tsv-sample-row rows = samples ID trait1 … tsv-sample-col rows = traits ID s1 s2 …

Files may be plain or gzip-compressed (detected from the file contents, not the extension), tab or whitespace separated. Values must be numeric and finite (inf is an error naming the trait and sample); missing values are spelled by missing_str (default NA).

Sample, trait, covariate and FID IDs must not contain whitespace or a double quote; anqchor rejects such IDs. anqchor hands qpgen tab-separated files, and qpgen does not strip quotes, so an ID such as "A" or A B would not match between the two (builds before qpgen 0.2.0 also split fields on any whitespace). A tsv-sample-col or tensorqtl header column with no numeric value at all is reported as a probable annotation column, not a sample.

prepare.dataset.<ds> writes prepare/datasets/<ds>/pheno.regenie.tsv.gz. A tab-separated regenie file with FID == IID and only NA as missing value is copied byte for byte; anything else is parsed and written with round-trip precision, so values are never rounded. The standalone equivalent is anqchor prepare pheno --in F --format tensorqtl --out F.tsv.gz.

Use identical sample IDs for cis and trans

pair-assoc and rect-assoc match phenotype and genotype samples by identical ID. The sample_map is used only by match. Run match first, then rename or drop samples in your phenotype and covariate files before running cis and trans.

Missing phenotype values

With qpgen 0.2.0, pair-assoc (the default cis engine) drops a sample with a missing phenotype from that trait's tests only. rect-assoc (the rect cis engine and trans) stops with an error on a missing value. anqchor does not check this before running qpgen: fill or remove missing phenotype values before running trans or cis --assoc-engine rect. dataset.json reports n_missing_values.

docs.title: Covariates
docs.text:
Optional (--cov, --cov-format), in any of the four layouts. The example covariates use the regenie layout (one row per sample); a file with one row per covariate is tsv-sample-col. prepare.dataset checks them and writes them in regenie layout to prepare/datasets/<ds>/cov.regenie.tsv.gz. Categorical covariates keep their text levels (sex stays XX/XY): qpgen encodes them itself when anqchor passes --cat-cov-names.

  • Empty cells are missing values, never a category level.
  • Numeric covariates must be numeric throughout: a column of mostly numbers with a few non-numeric cells (nan, .) is an error naming the first such cell; add the string to missing_str if it means "missing", or declare the covariate categorical. Infinite values are an error.
  • Categorical covariates are every column with a non-numeric value (detected automatically) plus the ones you name with --cat-cov-names (config: datasets.<ds>.cov_categorical). Name a covariate when its categories are coded as numbers, for example a batch number 1, 2, 3: without the flag it would be one numeric covariate with a linear effect. A non-numeric column with more than 20 levels (and more than a tenth of the samples) is an error unless named, since it would add one indicator column per level.
  • How qpgen encodes them (REGENIE --catCovarList semantics): a covariate with L levels becomes L − 1 indicator columns; the first level in sorted order is the reference (sex: XX reference, one XY indicator). Which level is the reference does not change any result. qpgen rejects a categorical covariate with more than 10 levels unless told otherwise (--max-cat-levels), so anqchor adds --max-cat-levels N when a covariate it uses has N > 10 levels.
  • Constant columns are dropped (they would be collinear with the intercept).
  • Missing values follow cov_missing: error (default), drop_samples (remove samples with any missing covariate) or impute_mean (the most frequent level for a categorical covariate). qpgen therefore never sees a missing covariate. Samples dropped by drop_samples are logged as warnings, recorded in dataset.json (n_samples_analysable, warnings) and shown in the cis and trans summaries.

Each qpgen command gets --cat-cov-names with the categorical covariates it uses: --cov-include sex,PC1-5 passes --cat-cov-names sex, --cov-include PC1-5,PEER1-10 passes none. prepare/datasets/<ds>/cov.json records the columns as written (raw_columns), the categorical covariates (categorical_names, categorical) and dropped columns (see outputs). Standalone:

anqchor prepare cov --in examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
    --format regenie --out results/cov.regenie.tsv.gz --json results/cov.json

wrote results/cov.regenie.tsv.gz: 729 samples x 66 covariates; categorical: sex ['XX', 'XY']
categorical covariates keep their text levels; use --cat-cov-names sex

Add --encode to write numeric indicator columns instead of text levels, for a tool without categorical support.

To use only some covariates of the file, name them with --cov-include (or cov: {include: [...]} in a configuration file). Ranges expand: --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 means sex, PC1…PC5, PEER1…PEER10. An unknown name stops the run with an error listing the available names (unknown covariate name(s) 'FOO'; available: sex, PC1-5, PEER1-60).

docs.title: Trait annotation
docs.text:
Trait loci are needed by trans (cell classes, trait_chroms) and by the rect cis engine's cross-chromosome controls. Sources, in order:

  1. trait_annot: a BED-like file (chrom start end id + anything, header optional, so a tensorQTL matrix works) or a trait chrom start end table with a header (column names such as trait/gene_id/phenotype_id and chr/chrom/chromosome are recognised). Without a header the layout is chosen by which column looks like a chromosome; when both or neither do (numeric trait IDs), anqchor asks for a header line;
  2. otherwise the phenotype file itself when it is in tensorqtl format.

Annotation IDs are matched to phenotype trait IDs directly, or with whichever trait-ID rule matches the most traits (a BED naming genes ENSG…5 matches expression IDs ENSG…5:WASH7P by before_colon). In the example data the IDs are identical. Chromosome names are rewritten to the genotype style. The cis window is measured from start. Result: prepare/datasets/<ds>/traits.tsv (trait chrom start end, NA for unknown loci).

docs.title: References
docs.text:
A pair file with a header, tab or whitespace separated, plain or gzipped:

trait                    variant          beta       se         pval
ENSG00000275993.3:SIK1B  21:6122794:C:T   -0.448959  0.0888711  8.054e-07
  • Columns are mapped with columns: {trait: …, variant: …, beta: …, se: …, pval: …}; pval is optional and only carried into the outputs. Other columns are ignored.
  • variant is CHROM:POS:REF:ALT and beta is the effect of the ALT allele: the PRS and the sign concordance test rely on it. Nucleotide alleles are upper-cased (a → A).
  • Rows with a malformed variant, an empty trait or a non-finite beta/se are dropped (n_invalid); repeated (trait, variant) rows keep the first (n_duplicates).
  • prepare.reference.<ref> checks every variant against the indexed pvar (tabix -R, or by streaming without tabix) and writes variants.tsv with a present flag. A reference with no present variant is an error (usually chromosome naming or genome build).

A trans reference may instead (or additionally) give variants:, a CPRA list with one variant per line (first column; a non-CPRA first line is treated as a header).

docs.title: Sample maps (match only)
docs.text: When omics sample IDs differ from genotype IDs, give sample_map: a table with a header geno_id pheno_id (either order; the older NWD_ID SAMPLE_ID header is accepted too), one row per omics sample. Rows naming IDs absent from the genotypes or the phenotypes are dropped and counted in dataset.json. Unmapped phenotyped samples are still scored and can become rescue candidates. cis and trans ignore the map; when some mapped samples do not have identical genotype and phenotype IDs, prepare logs a warning and adds it to dataset.json warnings (it does not fail, even with no identical IDs, because it does not know which pipelines will run).

docs.title: Trait maps
docs.text: When no trait-ID rule fits, give trait_map: a two-column file ref_trait pheno_trait without header (a ref_trait pheno_trait header line is tolerated). trait_id_rule: file:<path> is a shorthand for the same thing.

docs.title: Running
docs.text: Each analysis runs on its own, into its own run directory (--out). This page explains the commands, what a run directory holds, how to re-run, reproduce and compare runs, and what to do when something fails.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command What it does anqchor match run identity matching up to the summary tables (no HTML) anqchor match report --out DIR renders DIR/report/match.html from the tables; runs no analysis anqchor match all match run, then match report anqchor cis run replication of known cis pairs for one set of inputs, up to the summary tables anqchor cis compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR puts finished cis runs side by side; writes comparison tables and report/cis.html anqchor cis report --out DIR renders report/cis.html of a cis run or of a comparison; runs no analysis anqchor cis all cis run, then cis report on that run anqchor trans run replicated reference pairs (cis and trans), hotspots and inflation for one set of inputs, up to the summary tables anqchor trans compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR puts finished trans runs side by side; writes comparison tables and report/trans.html anqchor trans report --out DIR renders report/trans.html of a trans run or of a comparison; runs no analysis anqchor trans all trans run, then trans report on that run anqchor steps lists the steps of a run with their status; runs nothing

The top-level anqchor run and anqchor report (several analyses from one configuration file) are described in the command-line reference. This guide always runs one analysis at a time.

docs.title: run, report, all
docs.text:
run does the work: it checks the inputs, runs qpgen and writes summary tables (TSV and JSON). report reads only those tables and writes the HTML report. It takes about a second, never runs qpgen, and can be repeated as often as you like, for example after upgrading anqchor or with --plotlyjs cdn for a smaller file. all does both in one command.

D=examples/mage/data
IN=(--geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz
    --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz)
anqchor match run "${IN[@]}" --out results/match
anqchor match report --out results/match

(IN is a shell array, so the commands work in both bash and zsh.)

trans run, trans compare, trans report and trans all work like the cis commands below.

docs.title: Flags or a configuration file
docs.text: Every run/all command takes its inputs as flags (--geno-list, --pheno, --cov, --pairs, ...), which is the usual way. A configuration file (--config FILE) is optional; given together, flags override the file. Without --config, the dataset is called dataset and the reference reference (--dataset-name, --reference-name change that); these names appear in step names and paths such as match/dataset/.

docs.title: Evaluating alternatives: one run per setup
docs.text:
A cis run evaluates one set of inputs. To find out which covariates, normalisation, genotype set or reference works best, run each alternative into its own directory and compare the finished runs:

D=examples/mage/data
anqchor cis run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --out results/cis/nocov
anqchor cis run --geno-list $D/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno $D/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs $D/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --cov $D/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz --cov-include sex,PC1-5,PEER1-10 \
  --out results/cis/peer10
anqchor cis compare results/cis/nocov results/cis/peer10 --out results/cis/compare

compared 2 run(s): nocov, peer10
tables: results/cis/compare
cis report: results/cis/compare/report/cis.html

Each run takes about 6 seconds on the example data; the comparison about a second. Runs are labelled by their directory names; --label (once per run, in order) chooses other labels. --no-report writes the tables only, and anqchor cis report --out results/cis/compare renders the report later. The runs may differ in any input; the comparison also counts replication over the pairs tested in every run (the _common columns of strategies.tsv), so runs with different genotypes or references remain comparable. The cis use case walks through a full comparison.

trans works the same way: one trans run per setup (--cov-include, --rint), each into its own directory (the commands on the example), then trans compare RUN_DIR... --out DIR puts them side by side and writes report/trans.html; trans report --out DIR re-renders it. The trans use case walks through a full comparison.

docs.title: Parallel runs
docs.text:
Runs never share a directory, so independent runs can execute at the same time, for example in separate terminals, as background jobs (& and wait) or as separate cluster jobs. Two commands on the same run directory cannot: the second one stops at once with error: another anqchor command is running in DIR (exit code 2).

Within a run, -j N lets make run up to N independent steps at once. --threads N gives match-prs-pheno N threads; the other qpgen commands are single-threaded.

docs.title: How a run works
docs.text:
1. The configuration is built from the file and the flags, and validated; input files must exist (exit 2 otherwise). qpgentools is located (exit 4 if missing).
  2. The complete settings are written to <run>/anqchor.resolved.yaml (not by a dry run or anqchor steps when the file exists).
  3. anqchor builds the run's steps, writes one signature file per step (steps/<name>.json: inputs, outputs, commands and parameters) and a Makefile.
  4. make runs what is out of date. Progress lines look like [anqchor] running <step>; each step's output goes to logs/<step>.log.
  5. run.json is updated with provenance, and ran: ... lists the steps that ran.

The generated Makefile is plain GNU make (3.81 compatible). Each step's target is a stamp steps/<name>.done, touched after the step succeeds and all its outputs exist.

docs.title: Re-runs and invalidation
docs.text:
Running the same command again does nothing (ran: nothing (all steps up to date)). A step runs again when:

  • a parameter changed: its signature changes, and anqchor removes the stamps of that step and everything downstream. Changing --z-threshold of match run, for example, re-runs match.<ds>.qpgen and match.<ds>.summarize and nothing else;
  • an input file is newer than the step's stamp (make's usual rule);
  • one of its outputs was deleted: the step and everything downstream run again;
  • qpgen was rebuilt or anqchor upgraded: steps that run qpgen record the binary's sha256, and Python steps the anqchor version, so the affected steps run again.

--threads does not change results and changing it re-runs nothing.

To preview what a change would re-run, add --dry-run to the command with the changed setting. On the identity-matching run of the Quickstart:

anqchor match run \
  --geno-list examples/mage/data/geno/mage.pgen_list.tsv \
  --pheno examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_expr.chr21_22.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --cov examples/mage/data/pheno/mage_covariates.regenie.tsv.gz \
  --pairs examples/mage/data/reference/gtex_lcl_eqtl.chr21_22.tsv.gz \
  --out results/match --z-threshold 2.5 --dry-run
# (first the recipes make would run, then)
# dry run: would run: match.dataset.qpgen, match.dataset.summarize
# dry run: Makefile written to /…/results/match/Makefile

docs.title: Partial runs
docs.text:
Option Effect --dry-run write the Makefile, print which steps would run, run nothing; existing signatures, stamps and anqchor.resolved.yaml are not changed --until STEP run STEP and everything it needs, nothing downstream --only STEP re-run exactly STEP; every upstream step must be up to date (done), otherwise exit 2 --force re-run the requested steps and everything upstream -j N / --jobs N run up to N steps in parallel --keep-going continue with independent steps after a failure --dataset NAME with a multi-dataset configuration file: restrict to these datasets (repeatable) --strategy NAME with a configuration file that lists several strategies (cis, trans): restrict to these (repeatable)

--until and --only cannot be combined. Step names are those printed by anqchor steps. It needs a configuration file; the run's own anqchor.resolved.yaml works:

$ anqchor steps --config results/cis/peer10/anqchor.resolved.yaml --out results/cis/peer10
prepare.genotypes                  done     validate genotype files; write an absolute pgen list and the sample list
prepare.reference.reference        done     normalise reference reference and check which variants exist in the genotypes
prepare.dataset.dataset            done     convert dataset dataset to regenie layout, encode covariates, annotate traits
prepare.mapping.dataset.reference  done     map reference reference traits onto dataset dataset
cis.dataset.default.inputs         done     covariates/phenotypes for cis strategy default on dataset
cis.dataset.default.assoc          done     test the reference pairs on dataset with strategy default (qpgentools pair-assoc)
cis.dataset.summarize              done     replication of reference pairs on dataset by strategy
report.cis                         missing  cis report (report/cis.html)

run directory: /…/anqchor/results/cis/peer10   logs: /…/anqchor/results/cis/peer10/logs/<step>.log

Status is done (up to date), stale (an input or parameter changed) or missing (never run, or an output was deleted). steps always lists the report step. After cis run it is missing; after cis report it is stale, because cis report renders the page outside the step graph. Both are expected.

docs.title: The run directory
docs.text:
A run of one analysis (here cis run) writes:

results/cis/peer10/
├── anqchor.resolved.yaml          # complete settings of the run (defaults filled, paths absolute)
├── run.json                       # provenance (below)
├── Makefile                       # generated on every invocation
├── .anqchor.lock                  # held while a command runs in this directory
├── steps/<step>.json|.done|.seconds   # signatures, stamps, wall times
├── logs/<step>.log                # output of each step
├── prepare/
│   ├── genotypes/                 # pgen_list.tsv, samples.txt, genotypes.json
│   ├── references/<ref>/          # pairs.tsv.gz, variants.tsv, variants.present.txt, reference.json
│   └── datasets/<ds>/             # pheno.regenie.tsv.gz, cov.regenie.tsv.gz, cov.json, traits.tsv,
│       │                          # samples.txt, sample_map.tsv, dataset.json
│       └── ref.<ref>/             # trait_map.tsv, pairs.tsv.gz, variants.txt, traits.txt, mapping.json
├── cis/<ds>/                      # pairs.long.tsv.gz, strategies.tsv, traits.tsv, power_curve.tsv, summary.json
│   └── strategies/default/        # cov.regenie.tsv.gz, strategy.json, pair_assoc.tsv.gz
└── report/cis.html                # only after 'cis report' or 'cis all'

A match run has prs/<ref>/ and match/<ds>/ instead of cis/, and a trans run trans/<ds>/. A run of a single analysis writes no report/index.html. Every file is described in Output files.

docs.title: The comparison directory
docs.text:
cis compare writes a separate directory:

results/cis/compare/
├── runs.tsv                       # one row per compared run: label, directory, inputs, counts
├── strategies.tsv                 # one row per run: replication counts, relative N_eff
├── pairs.long.tsv.gz              # every pair of every run
├── traits.tsv  power_curve.tsv    # per-gene results, replication vs p-value threshold
├── summary.json                   # recommendation, warnings, comparability
├── compare.json                   # manifest: runs, labels, the compare command
├── settings/<label>.anqchor.yaml  # the exact settings of each compared run
└── report/cis.html

settings/ keeps a copy of each run's anqchor.resolved.yaml, so a comparison records how every run was made even after the run directories are deleted.

docs.title: Reproducing a run
docs.text:
anqchor.resolved.yaml holds every setting of the run, including those given as flags. To repeat a run exactly, into a new directory:

anqchor cis run --config results/cis/peer10/anqchor.resolved.yaml --out results/cis/peer10_again

The same works with a copy from a comparison (--config results/cis/compare/settings/peer10.anqchor.yaml) and for match and trans. Change one setting with a flag on top (--cov-include sex,PC1-5) to make a variant of the run. qpgen is found again by the usual discovery (qpgen.binary: null), so use the same qpgen build; run.json records which one was used.

anqchor.resolved.yaml is rewritten by every command that runs steps in the directory, so it always describes the settings of the current outputs. A --dry-run and anqchor steps leave an existing file unchanged.

docs.title: Logs and failures
docs.text:
Each step writes logs/<step>.log. When a step fails, anqchor prints the step name, the last lines of its log and the log path, then exits with code 3:

[anqchor] FAILED cis.dataset.default.inputs (exit 1); log: logs/cis.dataset.default.inputs.log
error in step cis.dataset.default.inputs: unknown covariate name(s) 'FOO'; available: sex, PC1-5, PEER1-60
error: run failed in step cis.dataset.default.inputs; log: results/cis/x/logs/cis.dataset.default.inputs.log

A failed step leaves no stamp behind. Fix the cause and run the same command again; the steps that already succeeded are not repeated.

-v/--verbose (a root option: anqchor -v cis run ...) turns on debug logging.

docs.title: Provenance: run.json
docs.text:
Rewritten after every invocation that is not a dry run:

Key Content schema_version 1 anqchor_version, python, platform, host environment config_sha256 sha256 of anqchor.resolved.yaml qpgen binary, sha256, and git_commit of the git checkout the binary sits in invocations the last 20 invocations: argv, started, finished, returncode step_seconds wall time of the last successful run of each step

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 success 2 configuration or validation error before any step ran (invalid YAML or keys, missing input file, unknown --dataset/--strategy/step name, --only with upstream steps not up to date, report on a directory without results), or the run directory is locked by another command 3 a step failed (the failing step and its log are printed) 4 qpgentools missing or unusable (anqchor qpgen build/check also use 4 for build failures and missing subcommands)

anqchor prepare ... utilities exit with 2 on input errors.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Effect ANQCHOR_QPGEN path to qpgentools (after --qpgen / qpgen.binary) ANQCHOR_MAKE make executable (default make) ANQCHOR_TABIX, ANQCHOR_BGZIP htslib tools (default: PATH, then the qpgen submodule's htslib)
